But if the cheese is of unknown origin, and it is not known that any such thing is in it, then eating it is permitted when it is sold in the market of the Muslims, just as one may eat the slaughtered meat sold there.

Everything whose eating is forbidden becomes permissible for the one in dire necessity, when he can find nothing else and fears for his life; and the one compelled by need may eat of it until he is satisfied, if he wishes.

Everything that serves as nourishment for man, the grains, the green herbs, what the earth brings forth, and all the fruits that neither harm nor kill, is lawful to eat. The flesh of camels, cattle, sheep, and all wild animals, together with their milk, is lawful, except for the beasts of prey that possess fangs and seize and devour other animals; their flesh, and nothing of them, is lawful to eat. All birds are lawful when slaughtered, except the birds of prey that possess talons and seize and devour other birds; eating them is not lawful, nor is eating their eggs.

If an egg is found and it is not known what creature it is from, it is examined: if its two ends differ, one pointed and one rounded, it is eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is eaten; but if its two ends are alike, it is not eaten, for that is the egg of a creature whose flesh is not eaten. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the eating of the rabbit, but disliked the lizard (al-dabb), the hedgehog, and the other creeping things of the earth.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is narrated that he permitted the use of vessels touched by impurity or wine once they have been washed and cleaned; and concerning food in which the small creatures of the earth, flies, and whatever has no blood happen to die, he said that this does not render the food forbidden to eat, nor does it make it impure. Whoever is repelled by it may leave it, and whoever wishes may eat. But if a creature possessing blood dies in it, then if the food is liquid it is spoiled, and if it is solid only what surrounds the dead creature is spoiled; whoever wishes may eat the rest, and there is no harm in it, once what lay around the dead thing has been removed and thrown away.

**On the Etiquette of Drinking**

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he forbade drinking in one continuous draft and commanded that one drink in sips, that the drinker name Allah at the first sip and praise Him when he has finished, and that he not breathe into the vessel. He should say "Bismillah" when beginning and "Alhamdulillah" when pausing. Ali (ع) said: "I observed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drinking water more than once, and he would breathe three times during the drink, taking the vessel away from his mouth at each breath, saying Bismillah when he began and Alhamdulillah when he paused." Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: "Three breaths in a drink are better than one."

He forbade drinking from the mouth of a waterskin, that is, bending back its opening and drinking directly from it, saying that this fouls it and carries the risk that a creature in the water, unseen by the drinker, might slip down his throat.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to drink both standing and sitting, yet he forbade lapping water straight from a river, a basin, a pond, or the like. When he saw a man doing so, he said to him: "You lap as a beast laps. If you find no vessel, drink from your hand, for it is the best of your vessels."

He also forbade gulping water down, saying: "Suck the water as it is sucked, and do not gulp it down as a burden upon yourself, for that brings on disease of the liver (al-kubad)." Yet he would gulp milk. Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) was seen gulping milk, and when he was asked, "Will you not take it in sips?" he answered: "Only the people of the Fire take it in sips." When he drank milk he would say: "O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it." When he drank water he would say: "Praise be to Allah, who has given us fresh, sweet water by His mercy, and has not given us bitter, briny water on account of our sins."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is narrated that he forbade drinking, or performing ablution, from the side of the handle (urwa) of the vessel.

**On What Is Permissible to Drink**

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Water is the master of drinks in this world and the Hereafter." Any naturally occurring water, in which no human labor has any part, is lawful and permitted to drink, provided it is not mixed with impurity and is neither harmful nor injurious. One may likewise drink the milk of every animal whose flesh is lawful to eat. It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said of camel's milk: "It draws from every tree." And he said (ع): "Cow's ghee is a cure, and its milk is medicine." A prophet once complained of a weakness he found in his body, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: "The finest meat is that taken with milk; eat them both, for I have placed strength in both of them." And it is said: "Meat and milk are the broth of the prophets." He said (ع): "Honey is a healing." Ali (ع) said: "No sick person was ever healed by the like of honey." And he said: "Can any of you not, when he falls ill, ask his wife to give him a dirham or two from her dowry, and buy honey with it, and drink it dissolved in rainwater?"

> وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ مُّبَرَكًۭا

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says regarding the dowry: ﴿فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا﴾, "If they willingly give up to you any part of it, then consume it in satisfaction and ease" (al-Nisa: 4); and He says regarding honey: ﴿فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾, "In it is healing for people" (al-Nahl: 69); and He says regarding rainwater: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُبَارَكًا﴾, "And We sent down from the sky blessed water" (Qaf: 9).

Water mixed with honey, milk, or anything similar is lawful to drink, as are drinks made from dates, raisins, or other sweeteners, so long as they have not changed. The same holds for everything pressed from grape juice, dates, raisins, or the fruits and herbs that are lawful to eat: drinking such juice is lawful as long as it has not turned, whether taken pure or mixed with water, and selling it, buying it, and benefiting from it are lawful likewise. So too if grape juice is cooked until it thickens without turning; it is lawful to drink, pure or mixed with water, as long as it does not change. It has been narrated of Ali (ع) that he used to provide the people with al-tila, which is grape juice boiled until it gains body and, if left, does not turn but becomes like honey; that and its like are lawful to drink, pure or mixed with water, as long as they do not change. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) was asked about drinking pressed juice, and he said: "There is no harm in it. Drink from a clean vessel that is not seasoned with wine; drink it as long as a large quantity does not intoxicate. But if a large quantity intoxicates, then a small quantity of it is forbidden. Do not drink what has stood a long while, for after an hour, or after a night, the pleasure of wine departs and only its sin remains. So fear Allah and call yourselves to account."

It was the mark of the Shia of Ali that they were known for piety, diligence, restraint, the shunning of sins great and small, and love for the friends of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It has been narrated from Ali (ع) that he said: "We used to soak raisins or dates in water in a clean vessel for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He would drink it that day and the next; and if it had changed by the third day, he ordered it poured away." This is the lawful drink that is called nabidh only because of what is cast, that is, thrown, into the water, of dates, raisins, or the like, which sweetens it when the water is brackish. But if it is left to ferment, so that it boils, intensifies, and throws up froth, then it is wine, and a large quantity of it is forbidden once it intoxicates.

**On What Is Forbidden to Drink**

> يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوٓا۟

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾, "O you who believe, intoxicants, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are but an abomination of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it, that you may be successful" (al-Maidah: 90). By this He forbade wine, just as He forbade all things unlawful.

It has been narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Wine is forbidden; no one drinks it in this world and then drinks it in the Hereafter, in the sacred enclosure of holiness (hazirat al-quds)." And he said: "Allah has cursed wine: its presser, the one who has it pressed, its seller, its buyer, its drinker, the one who serves it, the one who consumes its price, the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried." He said: "That which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity." He forbade treating illness with wine and intoxicants, and forbade that they be given to children or animals, saying that the sin falls upon whoever gives it to them.

It has been narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) that he said: "Intoxicating drink comes from five things: dates, raisins, wheat, barley, and honey, that is, besides grapes." And from Muhammad ibn Ali (ع), and upon his forefathers be peace, it is narrated: "The one addicted to wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the day he meets Him as one who worships an idol; and whoever drinks a single draft of it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not accept a prayer from him for forty nights."

From Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) it is narrated that he said: "Paradise is forbidden to three: the one addicted to wine, the worshipper of idols, and the enemy of the family of Muhammad." From Ali (ع) it is narrated: "Whoever drinks wine and dies within forty days of having drunk it meets Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as one who worships an idol." And he said (ع): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every intoxicant from every drink, and whatever the Messenger of Allah has forbidden, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden. Every intoxicant is forbidden, and that which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity."

A man from the people of Kufa said to him: "May Allah set you right; the jurists of our land say that only wine made from grapes is forbidden." He said to him: "O Sheikh, I do not know what the jurists of your land say. My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: That which intoxicates in large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity." Jafar ibn Muhammad then said (ع): "Taqiyya is my religion and the religion of my forefathers in everything except three matters: the prohibition of intoxicants, the removing of the two leather socks at ablution, and the saying aloud of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, meaning that it be recited aloud in the prayer."

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: "One must not treat illness with wine or intoxicants, nor may women use such a thing to dress their hair, for my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that Ali (ع) said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed no cure in any impurity that He has forbidden." He (ع) was also asked about drinking al-fuqqa, and when the questioner had described its nature, he said: "It is forbidden; do not drink it." And he (ع) said, concerning the seasoned vessels, that wine was not forbidden on account of such vessels, but that he had forbidden the intoxicant in little and in much alike; he only disliked the seasoned vessels because they alter the drinks.

**On What Makes Medicine Beneficial**

In this chapter we set down what has come from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), concerning medicine, the treatment and remedy permitted with it, and what they forbade in that regard, all of which falls within the gates of the lawful and the unlawful. It may be that one who doubts what has come from them, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), will deny it when he hears it; and if he uses it without true belief, he will find no benefit in it and so cast it aside. For Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brings benefit through it only to the people who affirm them and submit to their command, who receive what has come from them with acceptance, not to one who takes it as a mere trial, without belief, without intention, and without conviction.

What confirms this is the report narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع): Muhammad ibn Khalid, the governor of Medina, was recovering from an illness that had befallen him, and complained, in a gathering of people, of a pain he felt in his abdomen. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said to him: "Shall I not tell you a hadith my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Abu Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn told me, from his father, from his grandfather, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that a man complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a pain he felt in his abdomen. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Take a drink of honey and cast into it three grains of black seed (shuniz), or five, or seven, and you will be cured by the leave of Allah. He did so and was cured. So take this yourself."

A man of Medina who was present in the gathering objected and said: "O Abu Abd Allah, the hadith is sound, and we have heard it, but we tried it and gained no benefit from it." At this Abu Abd Allah (ع) grew very angry and said: "Allah brings benefit through this only to those who believe in Him and affirm His Messenger (ع), the Muslims who submit to his command and receive it from him with acceptance. As for the hypocrites who doubt it and do not affirm him, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not benefit them by it. Perhaps you are a hypocrite, and you took it without affirming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and so you were denied its benefit." The man fell silent, was overcome with shame, and bowed his head, and all who were present in the gathering affirmed the truth of Abu Abd Allah's words. We, for our part, cannot reckon how much of this we have used with sincere intention and certainty and have indeed benefited from it. So whoever turns to anything mentioned in the chapters of this section, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, seeking treatment and cure by it, let him turn to it with intention, sincerity, and certainty, for it will benefit him, if Allah wills. But if doubt over it has crossed his heart, he should not treat himself with its like; and if he inclines to the word of the physicians where they have spoken against it, then he will gain no benefit from it. It is Allah who grants the success of affirming His friends and submitting to their command, and of receiving and accepting from them, to those of His servants whom He is pleased with and chooses for their guardianship.

**On Seeking Healing Through Acts of Righteousness**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "In the black seed (al-habba al-sawda) is a cure for every disease except al-sam," that is, death. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said this to some of his companions, telling them this hadith, and it pleased them, and they said: "O son of the Messenger of Allah, how easy a remedy is this, that heals every disease but death!" He said: "Yes. Shall I not tell you of something easier still, in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ excluded neither death nor anything else?" They said: "What is it, O son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Supplication, for it turns back the decree even after it has been firmly sealed." And he joined his fingers together, all of them, bringing the two little fingers side by side, depicting the firm sealing of the decree.

It is narrated of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he missed a man of the Ansar, who came to him after a time, and he said: "What has kept you from us?" He said: "Sickness and poverty, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Shall I not teach you words to call upon Allah with, by which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will lift that from you?" He said: "Yes, by my father and my mother, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Say: There is no power and no strength except through Allah; I place my trust in the Living who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has taken no son, who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no protector from humiliation; and magnify Him greatly."

From Ali (ع) it is narrated that he said: "I complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a forgetfulness that had come over me, on account of which much of the Quran slipped away from me. He said to me: O Ali, I will teach you words that will drive that from you and fix the Quran firmly in your heart. Say: O Allah, have mercy on me through the forsaking of disobedience to You for as long as You keep me alive; have mercy on me by sparing me what does not concern me; grant me good discernment in what pleases You with me; bind my heart to the keeping of Your Book as You taught it to me; and grant that I recite it in the manner that pleases You."

Among the words he taught for the firm holding of revelation was this: by Your Book give light to my sight, release my tongue, open my chest with it, employ my body in it, and grant me strength through it, for none can grant strength in it but You. He said: I prayed with those words, and Allah established the Quran firmly in my chest.

It was narrated from him that he said: If one of you sets before him a vessel containing food or drink and fears that something in it may harm him, let him name Allah over it and take from it, for nothing harms alongside the name of Allah.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah, (ع), that a man among his companions complained to him of a corruption he found in his stomach, saying that he could eat no food without it harming and distressing him. He said to him: Say the name of Allah over every food you eat, and over every variety of it as you eat it, and it will not harm you. The man did so and was cured.

It was narrated from him that a man among his companions was struck with a whiteness between his eyes and complained of it, for the affliction had taken hold of him and grieved him. He said to him: You must make dua while you are in prostration. The man said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), teach me the words to pray with. He said: Say: O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Compassionate, O Hearer of prayers, O Giver of good things, grant me the good of the Hereafter and of this world, turn away from me the evil of them both, and remove from me this affliction that is between my eyes, for it has grieved and saddened me. He did so and was healed.

It was narrated from him that he said: Be eager for charity and give it early in the day, for there is no believer who gives a charity sincerely, desiring by it what is with Allah, except that Allah wards off from him the evil of what descends from the sky on that day, and shields him from it. Then he said: And do not think little of the prayers of the poor for the sick among you, for they are answered on your behalf, though they may not be answered for the poor themselves.

Ismail ibn Ali entered Medina while he was ill, and Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), came to visit him. When he saw his condition, he said to him: Call for a basket, put wheat in it, and set it before you. Then instruct your servants that when a beggar comes, they bring him in to you, and hand him some of that wheat with your own hand, and ask him to pray to Allah for you. He said: Shall I not rather give them dirhams and dinars? Abu Abd-Allah, (ع), said: Do what I have commanded you. He did so, and was granted health.

It was narrated from Abu Abd-Allah, (ع), that he said: Three things drive away forgetfulness and bring on remembrance: reciting the Quran, using the siwak, and fasting.

It was narrated from him that a man among his companions complained to him of how heavily he was overtaken by worry and grief. He said: When anything of that befalls you, pass your hand over the place of your prostration, then draw your hand across your face from the left side of your cheek, and across your forehead to the right side of your cheek, then say: In the name of Allah, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. O Allah, remove from me worry and grief. Let him do this three times.

It was narrated from him, (ع), that he said: Whoever says every day, thirty times, In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; and blessed be Allah, the best of creators; and there is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great, Allah will ward off from him ninety-nine kinds of affliction, the least of which is madness.

Mention of bearing illness with patience for its reward:

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, said: The groaning of the sick man, if he is patient and counts it for reward, is recorded for him as good deeds; but if it is in panic, he is called one given to panic, and there is no reward for him. The full treatment of this matter, and of the reward in illness for the one who is patient and counts it for reward, has its place among the chapters on funerals. It is also narrated from them, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah, (ع), with a son of hers who was afflicted in his mind, and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for this son of mine that He may heal him. He said: As you wish. If you wish, I will pray to Allah for him and He will heal him; and if you wish, I will leave him, and there will be no reckoning or punishment upon him. She said: Then leave him, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah's prayers and (ع).

Mention of seeking refuge and the ruqyah:

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, would seat al-Hasan and al-Husayn, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), upon his thighs and seek refuge for them, saying: I seek refuge for you both in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every crawling thing, and from every envious eye. And he would say: Thus did my father Ibrahim, (ع) and his family, seek refuge for his two sons Ismail and Ishaq, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ).

It was narrated from him, (ع), that Labid ibn al-Asam the Jew, and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah, worked sorcery against him in a cord of red and yellow threads in which they had tied eleven knots, then placed it inside the sheath of a date-palm and lowered it into one of the steps of a well in Medina. So the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, remained unable to hear, to see, to stand, to speak, to eat, or to drink. Then Jibril, (ع), descended with the two chapters of refuge and said to him: Labid ibn al-Asam and the Jewish woman Umm Abd-Allah have worked sorcery against you. He told him where the sorcery lay, and recited over him: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq, and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, to the end of the two chapters. As the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, recited, one knot was loosened and he sat up; he recited again and another knot was loosened, until he had recited eleven times and eleven knots were loosened, and the Prophet, (ع) and his family, sat up free of it. He ordered Ali, who brought him the sorcery from the well in which it had been placed, and he summoned Labid and Umm Abd-Allah and said: What moved you to do what you have done? Then he said to Labid: May Allah not bring you out of this world safe and sound. Labid was a man of wealth and great means. A boy passed by him wearing in his ear an earring worth a dinar, so he snatched it and tore the boy's ear and took it; and for this his hand was cut off and cauterized, yet the bleeding would not stop, and he bled until he died.

Ali, (ع), said: I fell gravely ill, so that I could find no rest upon my bed, and the Prophet, (ع) and his family, came to visit me. He said to me: O Ali, the most sorely tried of people in this world are the prophets, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Rejoice, for this is your share of the chastisement of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, together with the reward laid up for you. Then he said to me: Would you like Allah to lift from you what afflicts you? I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Say: O Allah, have mercy upon my thin skin and my fragile bone, and I seek refuge in You from the surge of the burning. O Umm Maldam, if you have believed in Allah, then do not eat flesh, do not drink blood, and do not boil over upon the mouth; depart instead to one who claims that there is another god alongside Allah. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. Ali, (ع), said: I said it, and I was healed at that very hour. Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: I never turned to it in distress but that I found it answered; and they used to teach it even to women and children.

It was narrated from Ali, (ع), that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, gave license for ruqyah by the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and by what is known of His remembrance and His names. He said: These incantations are among what Sulayman ibn Dawud, (ع), took as authority over the jinn.

It was narrated from him, (ع), that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, said: There is no ruqyah except in three things: a festering wound, an evil eye, or blood. People hold that the ruqyah is for the sting of the scorpion and the sting of the wasp, but that is a mistake. The hummah is the venom in such things, from the scorpion and the serpent and others; the hummah is a venomous creature, while the scorpion's sting is a needle.

It was narrated of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, that he sent out a company, and they passed by an Arab tribe whose chief had been stung. They asked whether anyone among them could perform a ruqyah, and one of them recited over him the Opening of the Book, and he was cured. When the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, was told of it, he approved it. One of his wives also performed a ruqyah with the two chapters of refuge, and he approved that, saying to her: And how did you know that it is a ruqyah?

He, may Allah bless him and his family, said: There is no contagion, no ill omen from birds, and no ham; but the evil eye is real and the good omen is real. And he, (ع) and his family, said: When one of you looks upon a person, or a beast, or anything pleasing that delights him, let him say: I have believed in Allah; may Allah bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad; then his eye will not harm what he looked upon. It was narrated from him, (ع), that when an eye struck him or a headache came upon him, he would spread out his two hands, recite into them the Opening of the Book and the two chapters of refuge, then wipe his face with them, and what he had been feeling would depart.

He, (ع) and his family, forbade sorcery, soothsaying, amulets, and tiwalah. Amulets are what is hung upon a person bearing other than the names of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and tiwalah is what women make to draw the love of their husbands to them. Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: There is no harm in a charm that is hung if it contains something of the Quran.

A man complained to Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), of a pain he found in himself. He said: Say In the name of Allah, and wipe over the place, then say: I seek refuge in the might of Allah, I seek refuge in the power of Allah, I seek refuge in the majesty of Allah, I seek refuge in the greatness of Allah, I seek refuge in all the bounds of Allah, I seek refuge in the names of Allah, and I seek refuge in the names of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family, from the evil of what I find. Let him say this seven times. The man said: I said it, and what I had been suffering left me.

It was narrated from him, (ع) and his family, that he said: When you wish to seek refuge, clasp your two palms together, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, He is Allah, One three times, then lay them upon the place of pain; then clasp them again, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of the Falaq three times, and lay them upon the pain a second time; then clasp them again, recite into them the Opening of the Book and Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind three times, and lay them upon the pain. Three times in all.

It was narrated from Ali, (ع), that he said: Whoever is ill-tempered, let the call to prayer be given in his ear. And Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said of the sick man who has a ruqyah performed for him: There is no harm in it, so long as the ruqyah is by something known. It was narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), that he said: When you wish to perform a ruqyah upon a wound, against pain, or blood, or what is feared for it, place your hand upon the wound and say: In the name of Allah I perform your ruqyah; in the name of Allah the Greatest, against iron and stone, and the dark fang and the running of sweat, so let it not deceive, and against the eye, so let it not keep vigil. Repeat it three times.

Mention of treatment and medicine:

We have narrated from the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, was asked whether the sick should be treated and given remedies. He said: Yes. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has sent down no disease without sending down a remedy with it, so seek treatment, except for the sam, which is death, for it has no cure.

A group of the Ansar asked him about a man among them who complained of his stomach, and about a Jewish physician who treated such a thing by opening the abdomen. The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, was reluctant and did not permit them. They returned to him about it two or three times, and each time he refused them, until at last he said to them: Do as you wish. So the Jew was called for, and he opened the man's abdomen, removed a great deal of foul matter from it, then washed the abdomen, stitched it, and treated it, and the man became well. When the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, was told of it, he said: He who created the disease has appointed for it a remedy; and the best of remedies are cupping, phlebotomy, and the black seed, which is the shuneez. And the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, forbade imposing strict diets upon the sick.

He looked at Salman, who was eating dates while suffering from sore eyes, and said: O Salman, you eat dates while you have sore eyes? Salman said: O Messenger of Allah, it is only my right eye that is sore, and I am chewing with my left teeth. So the Messenger of Allah smiled and did not stop him.

It was narrated from him, (ع) and his family, that he said: To forgo the evening meal is a cause of weakness in old age. And he said, (ع) and his family: Do not force your sick to eat, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic feeds them and gives them drink. It was narrated from him, (ع) and his family, that there is no harm in an enema, were it not that it enlarges the belly. And he said, (ع) and his family: When blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him draw it off, even with a small blade, meaning when the blood overcomes him. And he said, (ع) and his family: Cupping of the head is a cure for every disease, and remedy lies in four things: cupping, the enema, the depilatory, and vomiting.

Ali, (ع), said: The Messenger of Allah was never seized by fever but that he turned to cupping. And he used to say: When blood becomes excessive in one of you, let him be cupped on whatever day it may be, and let him recite Ayat al-Kursi, seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family. Do not hold certain days to be against you, lest they be set against you; be cupped on whichever of them you wish; and let him name Allah over the cupping vessel.

Among the things narrated concerning the body and its remedies is the matter of cupping: the cupping of the head brings relief, and the cupping of the upper back, the kahil, is beneficial. As for fever, it is from the heat of Hell, so it is to be cooled with water; and when the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) was taken with fever, he would call for water and place his hand in it.

Al-Hasan and al-Husayn (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) once fell ill with fever, and Fatima came to the Messenger of Allah seeking help and refuge. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah for your son that He heal him, for he is gravely ill." So the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) rose and came to him, sat at his head, and found him in a heavy state. He said, "O Fatima, it is Allah the Almighty who bestowed him upon you, and He is able to heal him." Then Jibril (ع) came to him and said, "O Muhammad, Allah the Almighty has not sent down upon you a sura of the Quran in which there is not a fa, and every fa is an affliction, an afa, save al-Hamd, for there is no fa in it. So call for a cup of water, recite al-Hamd over it forty times, then pour it over him, and Allah the Almighty will heal him." The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) did so, and it was as though the boy had been loosed from a tether.

It is narrated from him (ع) that he was asked about cauterisation, and he forbade it. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said, "There is no objection to cauterisation. As for what was forbidden, that concerns what is feared to cause death or what disfigures the creation. As for what one hopes will bring a cure, there is nothing wrong with it."

The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) used to command applying kohl with ithmid before sleep, and he would say, "Apply kohl an odd number of times." And he said, "You must use ithmid, for it makes the lashes grow, removes the motes from the eye, and clears the sight." He said ((ع) and his family), "Al-Ajwa is from Paradise, and in it is a cure for poison." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) described its preparation thus: one takes Ajwa dates, removes their stones, pounds them thoroughly, and kneads them with aged cow's ghee; then it is set aside, and when it is needed by one who has taken poison, it is eaten and benefits him.

It is narrated from him (ع) that a scorpion stung the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family). He struck it down and said, "May Allah curse you, for you spare neither believer nor disbeliever from your sting." Then he called for salt, placed it upon the place of the sting, and pressed it with his thumb until it dissolved, and said, "If people knew what is in salt, they would have no need of any antidote alongside it."

It is narrated from him (ع) that he said, "Whoever eats twenty-one seedless raisins each morning on an empty stomach will not fall ill except with the illness in which he dies." And, "Whoever eats seven dates at his bedtime will be spared colic, and the worms in his belly will be killed." He said (ع) to Jafar ibn Abi Talib (ع), "Eat quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the coward."

He said, "Honey is a healing." Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said that Allah the Almighty has mentioned it in His Book, where He said of it, "فِيهِ شِفَآءٌۭ لِّلنَّاسِ," that is, "In it is a healing for people." He said ((ع) and his family), "Beware of al-shabram, for it is hot; and you must take senna, so treat yourselves with it, for if anything could repel death, senna would repel it. And treat yourselves with fenugreek, for if my nation knew what it holds for them, they would treat themselves with it even were it to cost its weight in gold." He forbade ((ع) and his family) the eating of clay and charcoal, and said that Allah the Almighty created Adam from clay and therefore forbade the eating of clay to his descendants. "Whoever eats clay has aided in his own harm, and whoever persists in eating clay until he dies of it, I will not pray over him." Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said that the eating of clay breeds hypocrisy.

The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said that eating fresh, soft fish dissolves the body, so one should not become accustomed to it; and when he ate it he would say, "O Allah, bless it for us and give us in its place what is better than it." Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said, "Whoever eats fish, let him eat dates afterward, for that removes its harm." The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade the drinking of al-hamim. Al-hamim is the rain that falls in the severity of heat, and al-hamim is also hot water; likewise the rainwater that falls in intense heat and runs along the ground until it grows hot and harmful. For this reason he forbade its drinking, not because it is unlawful or impure, but because it was disliked for the harm it causes.

It is narrated from him (ع) that he said, "Whoever is a physician, or one who undertakes treatment, whether Arab or non-Arab, let him not treat anyone until he has obtained a written release from him, witnessed by witnesses. Let him fear Allah the Almighty, strive diligently, and counsel sincerely." By the release he meant that the physician should be learned in medicine and should not treat people while ignorant; for if he does, he is liable for what he destroys.

It is narrated from him (ع) that he used to say, "Whoever desires to endure, though there is no enduring, let him lighten his burden, keep to his sandals, take his morning meal early, draw near his evening meal, and lessen intercourse." It was said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the lightening of the burden?" He replied, "It is debt."

He said (ع), "The truffle is from the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye." Some of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) described its preparation: one takes a truffle and washes it until it is clean, then squeezes its water into a vessel and kindles a fire beneath it until it thickens; then musk is added to it, and it is applied as kohl for all the ailments of the eye. When its moisture dries, it is moistened with rainwater from the sky and applied as kohl. And it is narrated from Ali (ع) that he said, "Nothing restores the woman in childbirth like the eating of fresh, moist dates. Allah the Almighty fed Maryam fresh dates in her childbirth." He said (ع), "Eat the pomegranate with its pith, for it is a tanner for the stomach. And you must eat apples, for they cleanse the stomach."

It is narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said, "Celery is the herb of the prophets, and there is no leaf of endive but that upon it is water from Paradise. You must take the gourd, for it strengthens the heart and the mind." He ((ع) and his family) once trod upon the scorching ground and it burned him, so he stepped onto the purslane, which is the foolish herb, and the heat of the scorching ground subsided for him; so he blessed it, and he used to eat it and was fond of it. Ali (ع) said, "The sick are healed by nothing like the drinking of honey."

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about a man who seeks treatment from a Jew or a Christian. He said, "There is nothing wrong with that, for healing is in the hand of Allah the Almighty." He was also asked: if a woman has a disease in her body, or a fracture or a wound in a place that is not proper to look upon, may she uncover it to a man who treats her? He said, "There is nothing wrong with that when she is compelled to it." And Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about a man who treats people with medicine and takes a fee for it, and he said, "There is nothing wrong with it."

It is narrated from him (ع) that he said, "If people were moderate in their food and drink, their bodies would remain sound." He said (ع), "Abandoning the evening meal is the ruin of the body." He said, "Allah the Almighty says, وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةًۭ وَعَشِيًّۭا, that is, and they shall have their provision therein, morning and evening." A man complained to him of pains and indigestion that he was suffering, and he said, "Take your midday meal and your evening meal, and eat nothing between them, for that is the corruption of the body." He said, "Abandoning the evening meal diminishes a strength that does not return," and, "Let not the aged man abandon the evening meal, even if it be only a morsel." He said (ع), "Eating meat with milk makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone." And he said (ع), "A prophet among the prophets complained to Allah the Almighty of his few children, so He commanded him to eat meat with eggs."

It is narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) counseled Ali (ع), saying, "O Ali, sleep upon your back, for it slims your belly; and drink water by sipping, for thereby your food is made wholesome. Wear a ring, and apply kohl an odd number of times, for it will brighten your sight. Anoint yourself every other day, in keeping with the Sunnah of your Prophet. Renew your sandals, for they are the anklets of a man, and turbans are the crowns of the Arabs. When you cook a pot, make its broth plentiful, for if your neighbors do not receive some of its meat, they will receive some of its broth. Wear a ring of ruby and carnelian, for it is fortunate and blessed; whenever a man looks at his face within it, it increases him in light, and the prayer offered wearing it is worth seventy prayers. Wear the ring upon your right hand, for that is the practice of the Messengers, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. Do not wear a ring upon the left, nor of anything but ruby and carnelian."

It is narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) that a man among his companions complained to him of pain in his loin. He said to him, "Take what falls from the table among the food, follow after it, and eat it." The man said, "I did so, and I was healed." Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said, "Eat of the food that falls from the table, for in it is a healing, by the leave of Allah the Almighty, for whoever seeks healing by it, that is, for every disease." A man looked at apples in the hands of Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع), and he said to him (ع), "The apple cools the heat and quenches it, and removes the fever." He mentioned vinegar (ع) and said, "It firms the mouth and kills the worms of the belly." He said (ع), "Rice sawiq, when it is parched and ground, binds the belly; if part of it is made into sawiq and part into a gruel, it binds the belly. Sawiq makes the flesh grow and strengthens the bone, and it benefits the feverish one when it is moistened and washed three times. Take sawiq dry on an empty stomach, for it dispels phlegm and bile." And it is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn (ع) that he permitted treatment with the milk of she-asses, and that if one finds the milk of the wild ass, that is better.

The Body's Portion: Food, Drink, and Healing

The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), was asked about a man whom fear of Allah Almighty had so overtaken that he abandoned women, abandoned wholesome food, and grew unable to lift his head toward heaven out of reverence for Allah Almighty. The one who put the question said, "As for his turning away from women, I know what the Messenger of Allah, (ع), had of them. And as for his turning away from wholesome food, the Messenger of Allah, (ع), used to eat meat and honey. And as for the fear of Allah Almighty entering him until he could no longer raise his head toward the sky out of reverence, who was ever more fearful of Allah, or more humbled before Him, than the Messenger of Allah, (ع), yet he did not do this?" For Allah Almighty has said, *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example,"* and true humility is in the heart.

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

This is the spirit in which the merits of marriage are to be understood, for there is no monasticism in Islam. Allah Almighty said: *"And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."*

It is narrated from the Imams of the House of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), that he said: "Whoever loves to follow my way among my nation, let him know that marriage is one of my Sunnahs." And he said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah pure and purified, let him meet Him with a wife." And he said: "There is no young man who marries in his youth except that his devil cries out, Woe to him, he has protected two-thirds of his religion! So let the servant then fear Allah Almighty in the remaining third." Whenever he learned that one of his companions had married, he would say, "He has completed his religion." And he said, (ع), "The more a believer increases in faith, the more he loves women." And he said, "There is no monasticism in Islam. Marry, for I shall boast of your numbers before the nations." He forbade celibacy and the forsaking of marriage.

He said: "When a believing man comes to his believing wife, two angels enfold him, and he is like one who has drawn his sword in the path of Allah. When he is done, his sins fall from him as the leaves fall from the tree, as though he had washed himself clean of sin. If she conceives by him, he has the reward of one who fasts and stands in prayer. When the pangs of labor seize her, no one knows her reward but Allah Almighty. When she delivers, with every draft of milk she suckles the child Allah Almighty writes for her a good deed and erases from her an evil one. And if she should die of her travail, she will rise on the Day of Resurrection without reckoning, for she died of her affliction."

And he said: "Whoever abandons marriage out of fear of household expense has thought ill of his Lord the Almighty, who says, *If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty."* And he said: "Whoever amasses wealth and does not marry, so that the women left unwed because of him fall into sin, their sin rests upon him." And from Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع): "No two believers are joined in a lawful marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has wedded such a one to such a one; and no two believing spouses are parted from a marriage but that a caller from heaven cries out, Allah Almighty has permitted the separation of such a one from such a one."

On what is recommended in a spouse, and from whose marriage one should turn away, it is narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, that he said: "Choose well for your seed, for the maternal uncle is one of the two who share the bed." By this he meant: do not place your seed except in purity, that the mother of the child be not of corrupt origin nor corrupt in herself. From this also he forbade that a child be suckled by the milk of a wicked woman; and if such a thing is disliked in nursing and forbidden, then in lineage it is graver still and more emphatic. He said: "Marry those who are your equals, and give your daughters in marriage to them, and choose well for your seed."

He related that Allah Almighty says: "When I wish to grant My servant the good of this world and the Hereafter, I give him a tongue that remembers Me, a humble heart, a body patient in affliction, and a believing wife who gladdens him when he looks upon her and guards herself and his wealth in his absence." And he said: "Five things are of happiness: a righteous wife, upright children, righteous companions, a man's provision in his own land, and love for the family of Muhammad, (ع) and his family."

He said: "A good woman among women is like the albino crow, and the albino crow is seldom found." By "good" here he meant the believing, chaste, beautiful woman, fitting in all her states; and rare is the woman found in such a condition, so he likened her to the albino crow, which is the rarest of birds. He said: "A woman of standing has no price, neither the good among them nor the bad. As for the good, she has no price in gold or silver or all the possessions of this world; and as for the bad, she has no price, not even of dust, for dust is better than she." And he said: "The world is but enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is a righteous wife." And he said: "Of the believing man's happiness is a righteous wife, a spacious dwelling, an easy mount, and a righteous child."

He forbade that a woman be married for her wealth or her beauty alone, saying, "Her wealth makes her overbearing, and her beauty destroys her." And he said: "Take the one of religion." And he said, comparing what is most prized: "There is no horse finer than the deep black, and no woman like the daughter of one's age." And he said: "The best of your women are the women of Quraysh, the most tender toward a husband and the most devoted to a child."

He said: "Marry the one of clear, healthy complexion, for there is blessing in that. And when one of you would marry a woman, let him ask about her hair as he asks about her face, for the hair is one of the two beauties. And keep to those of shorter stature, for that is better suited to what you seek." He said: "A woman is but a necklace, so let each of you consider well with what he adorns himself." And he said: "If there is ill fortune in anything, it is in a woman, a dwelling, and a mount."

He said: "Women are four: a gathering that gathers, a spring that gives water, a war that subdues, and a galling fetter." As for the galling fetter, the people of the Age of Ignorance would shackle their captives and those they wished to torment with a thong of fresh hide stripped from a camel, turning the hair inward against the skin and binding it fast; as it dried it tightened and the skin contracted, and lice would breed within it and could not be reached because of its tightness, so the captive suffered greatly, a torment that struck without a blow. This the Prophet, (ع), made a likeness of the bad wife and what her husband endures from her. The gathering that gathers is she in whom is gathered her goodness and her purity; the spring that gives water is she who has a child in her arms and another in her womb; and the war that subdues is she of ill manners toward her husband.

> وَلَدٌۭ ۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌۭ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم ۚ مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍۢ ۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌۭ يُورَثُ كَلَلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌۭ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌۭ فَلِكُلِّ وَحِدٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ ۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ ۚ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍۢ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّۢ ۚ وَصِيَّةًۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌۭ

He said: "Beware of marrying the foolish woman, for her companionship is an affliction and her child is a loss." And he said: "The best women of my nation are those fairest of face and lightest in dowry." And he said: "Among the blessings of a woman is that her firstborn be a girl." He said again: "Women are four: a spring that gives water, a gathering that gathers, a war that subdues, and a barren woman." And he said: "Marry the dark-complexioned woman who is fertile, and do not marry the beautiful barren woman, for I will boast of your numbers before the nations on the Day of Resurrection. The children who die young are beneath the Throne of the Most Merciful, seeking forgiveness for their parents; Ibrahim, (ع), takes them into his care, and Sarah raises them upon a mountain of musk and amber and saffron."

He said: "The best of your women is the ardent yet chaste one, ardent toward her husband and chaste from all besides him." And he said: "Marry the virgins, for they are sweetest of mouth, purest of womb, quickest of the women to learn, and most steadfast in affection." And he said: "Marry the ayyami," meaning Allah Almighty will better their character, broaden their provision, and increase their blessing. His command here is to marry the ayyami, those women who once had husbands who died or who divorced them, and it is a command of encouragement, not of obligation that may not be left, just as Allah's word, *"And marry the unmarried among you,"* is of this kind. Whoever marries one of the ayyami, desiring what Allah Almighty and His Messenger have urged, has done what he was called to; and whoever marries a virgin, there is no fault in that, for the virtue of marrying virgins has already been mentioned from the Messenger of Allah. Yet the ayyami should not be passed over out of mere preference or disdain on account of a prior marriage, for most of the wives of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), had been married before, and Allah Almighty says: *"Indeed in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example for those who hope for Allah and the Last Day."*

> إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ

A Muslim should answer his Muslim brother who proposes to him, when he is satisfied with the man's religion; and he warned that if this is not done, there will be strife in the land and great corruption. He forbade a marriage sought for other than the face of Allah Almighty and chastity, and he forbade marriage undertaken for show and reputation. He said: "Whoever marries a woman for her standing or her wealth, Allah leaves him to that; but whoever marries her for her religion and her excellence, Allah Almighty grants him beauty and wealth besides." Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty: *"If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing, Knowing."* And he said: "There is no calamity heavier upon a servant in his religion than that his Muslim kinsman should come to him and say, Marry me your daughter, and he answer, I will not, because he is wealthier than the suitor."

It is told of Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), that he passed by a woman in one of the districts of Makkah and was struck by her beauty and character. He inquired about her, found her without a husband, proposed to her, married her, and consummated the marriage. Afterward a man of his kin came to him and said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, something has weighed upon me concerning your marriage to this woman that I could not bear, for you married her without asking after her lineage. I could not rest until I inquired, and I found her to be of the Banu Shayban, of the noblest of her people, and so I was gladdened and set at ease." Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), said, "And what was it you had feared?" The man said, "I feared she might not be your equal, and that people would speak of it." Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), said to him, "I had thought you of sounder judgment than this. Do you not know that Allah Almighty brought Islam and by it raised the lowly, completed the deficient, and ennobled what was base? There is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance."

He, (ع), also married the freedwoman who had borne a son to a man now dead. When Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan heard of it, he wrote reproaching him, thinking he had found in it a fault, and saying, "Was there not enough for you among the women of Quraysh and the noble Arabs to keep you from the mother of another man's son?" Ali ibn al-Husayn, (ع), wrote back to him: "To proceed: Allah Almighty has by Islam raised the lowly and completed the deficient, so there is no reproach upon the affair of a Muslim; reproach belongs only to the Age of Ignorance. And the Messenger of Allah, (ع), married such a one," meaning Safiyyah bint Hayy ibn Akhtab, "and in him is a good example." Were it permissible to disdain the mothers of children, the marriage bed would be abandoned and corruption would appear in the land; and the Imams, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), are the most fit to make this plain, that the people might follow their example.

Allah Almighty said: *"O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honored of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware."*

On the day of the conquest of Makkah he addressed the people, praised and glorified Allah, then said: "O people, Allah Almighty has taken from you the arrogance of the Age of Ignorance and its boasting in forefathers. You are all from Adam, and Adam was from clay. The best of Allah's servants before Allah are those most fearful of Him. Arabness is not a thing born of a father; it is a tongue that speaks. Whoever is held back by his deeds, his lineage will not advance him." And every claim of blood or rancor from the Age of Ignorance is beneath his feet until the Day of Resurrection.

It is told that he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib in marriage to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and said that he married her to al-Miqdad only that marriage might be made humble, that the people might follow the example of the Messenger of Allah, (ع), and that they might know that the most honored of them before Allah is the most God-fearing. Al-Zubayr was the brother of Abd Allah, the father of the Prophet, (ع), by both father and mother. Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: "The Messenger of Allah, (ع), married Qurayshi women to freedmen: he gave Dubaa bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib to al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and he married Tamim al-Dari to a woman of the Banu Hashim ibn Abd Manaf."

The Messenger of Allah, (ع), said: "When one whose religion and trustworthiness are pleasing to you comes seeking marriage, then marry him; for if you do not, there will be strife in the earth and great corruption."

It is narrated from Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), that he was in Makkah when word reached him that Dawud ibn Ali had ordered the killing of al-Maali ibn Hunaish, who was one of his own companions, and that he had been killed. Al-Sadiq, (ع), rose in anger, dragging his garment behind him. His son Ismail, (ع), came to meet him and said: "O my father, where are you going? The people are defiant, and their insolence against Allah Almighty is such as you well know. Leave them be." But he struck him upon the chest and said: "Step aside from me. Were it a blazing fire, I would plunge into it." He went on until he came in upon Dawud and said: "O Dawud, you have committed a sin that Allah will never forgive you." Dawud said: "And what is that?" He said: "You have killed a believing man from among the people of Paradise."

Dawud grew angry and fell silent for a time, then said: "And you too have committed a sin that Allah Almighty will not forgive you." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Your daughter has been given in marriage to a man from Banu Umayyah." Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), answered that in this his example was the Messenger of Allah himself, (ع), for he had given his daughter Zaynab in marriage to Abu al-As ibn Rabiah, and he had given Umm Kulthum in marriage to Uthman ibn Affan, and when she died he married him to Ruqayyah, both being his daughters, (ع) and his family.

Then he said: "You are the one who forbade the killing of believers unjustly." Dawud said: "I did not command that he be killed." Al-Sadiq said that al-Sarraqi had reported, "We have lost him," and that he, the killer, had said, "I have taken responsibility for him." So Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), had his companions seize the man and proceed with him to be put to death. The man cried out: "O servants of Allah, do you command me to kill men for them, and then exact retribution from me?" Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: "As for you, O enemy of Allah, you confess to the killing, and your companion has denied that he commanded you to it. Have you any proof of that?" The man said: "And who will bear witness for me against Dawud?" He said: "Then retribution from you is obligatory and must be exacted." And he delivered him over to the kinsmen of al-Maali, and they put him to death.

It was said to Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع): Is it permissible to give daughters in marriage to those of opposing views? He answered that the Messenger of Allah, (ع), had given his daughters in marriage to certain men whom they knew, and that Umar had sought the hand of Ali's daughter Umm Kulthum, (ع), and Ali had refused him. So Umar went to al-Abbas and complained of this to him, and pressed the Banu Abd al-Muttalib hard. Al-Abbas came to Ali, (ع), and said: "O son of my brother, you see the situation we are in. Umar has sought her hand and has pressed us hard over your refusing him." He did not cease until Ali committed her affair to him, and al-Abbas gave her in marriage to Umar on his behalf. It is therefore better to give daughters in marriage to people of sound faith, or to those who do not stir up enmity against the family of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family. The marriage of a believer is better than the marriage of any other, yet when there is necessity there is no harm in marrying people of differing views from among the Muslims. Likewise to marry among them is not forbidden, as marriage to polytheists is forbidden, but the meritorious and preferred course is marriage among people of sound faith, and after them the weak ones who are neither loyal nor hostile.

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

A man asked Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), about a sister of his wife, a believing woman of knowledge who was in Basra and had no man among her kin to oversee her affair. He said to him, (ع): "Do not give her in marriage to them. As for yourselves, there is no harm in your giving the weak women in marriage; but a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib, no." Zurara ibn Ayan asked Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), about the like of this, and he was permitted to give the weak women in marriage, but not a Nasibiyyah, the daughter of a Nasib. And Abu Jafar, (ع), said to Zurara ibn Ayan concerning the weak women: "Keep to the simple and weak among women." And Abu Jafar, (ع), said: "Marry into the people of doubt, but do not give your women to them in marriage, for a woman takes from her husband's manners, and he prevails over her in the matter of his religion."

He said, (ع): "The marriage of people of knowledge, and marriage among them, is foremost and best and nearest to Allah Almighty. If that is not to be had, then the weak ones who are neither loyal nor hostile are better than the people of enmity." After them come the Muslims of the people of truce, whom the Shariah binds together: they marry one another and inherit from one another, and the testimony of one of them concerning another is admissible when they are upright and not suspect. As for the people of disbelief, such as Jews, Christians, and polytheists, it is not lawful for any of them to marry a Muslim woman, though their marrying one another is permissible, and Muslim men may marry their women when there is necessity and Muslim women are not to be found. Muslim women, however, are not lawful for them.

Abu Abd Allah, (ع), was asked about the saying of Allah Almighty: ﴿الزَّانِي لَا يَنْكِحُ إِلَّا زَانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَالزَّانِيَةُ لَا يَنْكِحُهَا إِلَّا زَانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ وَحُرِّمَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress shall not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers." He said: "This was revealed concerning women known for licentiousness in the time of ignorance, who were openly hired out for adultery and had set up houses marked for that purpose. The truce came with the provision that whoever wished might return to them; among them were Habibah, al-Rabab, and Sarah, whose blood the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, declared lawful on the day of the conquest of Makkah, because she had been inciting the polytheists to fight the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family. As for a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, there is no harm in purchasing her and having relations with her, and there is likewise no harm in marrying such a woman when there is necessity, provided one is fortified and guarded against her. Yet chaste women are better and more fitting."

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a woman who does not turn away the hand of one who touches her, and I love her." He said: "Then keep her." It was narrated of a man who saw his wife committing adultery yet was loath to part from her: he may keep her if he wishes. (ع) was asked about a man's marrying an immoral woman, and he said: "What prevents him? But if he does so, let him fortify the door of his house." He was asked about a man who marries a slave girl born of adultery, and he said: "There is no harm in it, though to keep clear of that is dearer to me." Concerning a man who has a slave girl who has fallen into fornication, asking whether he may have relations with her, he said: "Yes, if he wishes." Concerning a man who marries a woman without full discernment, he said: "It is permissible, so long as no fault remains attached to his child." Concerning a child of adultery, whether one may have relations with her and sell her if she is a slave girl, and buy her, he said: "Yes; the forbidden does not render the lawful forbidden, nor corrupt it. Were people to turn away from the like of these and forbid their marriage, corruption in the land would multiply, and Allah may yet set right the corrupters and accept the repentance of the sinners."

Some of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), were asked about the saying of Allah Almighty, "The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist." He said: "The word marry here may mean the act of union and intercourse, or it may mean the contract and marriage. If it means union and intercourse, then it may indeed signify adultery, not lawful marriage." He said: "As for His words, except an adulterer or a polytheist, a man does not bring upon himself the wrath of Allah Almighty in this except while he is a polytheist." And the Messenger of Allah, (ع), said: "The adulterer does not commit adultery at the moment of his adultery while he is a believer."

**Mentioning the Seeking of Women's Hands in Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the household of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and upon the Imams of his house, that he forbade a man to propose marriage over the proposal of his brother, and to bid over the bid of his brother. Some of the Ahl al-Bayt, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), explained this and said: The meaning of the words of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, that a man should not propose over his brother's proposal, is that this is after there has come about mutual approach, contentment, inclination, attentiveness, and agreement, such that nothing remains but the contract itself. As for what falls short of that, there is no harm in two men, or a group, proposing to a woman until she inclines to one of them and answers him; only then is it disliked for another to oppose him with a proposal. In the same way it is permissible for a man to bid on a commodity and to purchase it, and for another to bid above him, so long as the two parties to the sale have not yet reached agreement.

The Messenger of Allah, (ع), commanded selling by open auction, and people have continued to this day to outbid one another in the call and otherwise, each raising upon the other until the commodity is settled and the seller accepts a buyer; after that no further bid should be made, nor any raising upon what has been commanded. It is a matter of recommendation, on account of the benefit in it. Should a suitor propose, or a bidder raise his bid upon a commodity, after agreement and before the contract of marriage or sale is concluded, that falls under the same ruling: if one surpasses another in merit before the contract is concluded, it does not invalidate the marriage or the sale, since nothing has become binding to another by contract. And the Messenger of Allah, (ع), said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, let him cast his gaze upon her, for he is but a buyer." And he said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, there is no harm in his looking at what draws him to her."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: I mentioned this hadith to Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, and he said to me: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, (ع). I sought the hand of a young woman from among the women of the Ansar, and I concealed myself for her behind a wall of her father's garden, and I looked at her and saw what I wished to see and what I had not meant to see, and she pleased me, so I married her, and she was the best of women."

> قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا۟ مِنْ أَبْصَرِهِمْ

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: There is no harm for one who wishes to marry a woman in looking at her; but he should not look at a slave girl except with her master's permission, meaning that the master may not wish to sell his slave girl or to offer her. The command from the Messenger of Allah, (ع), permitting a man to look at the woman he intends to marry, extends the permission of that gaze, once he has come to know that they will give her to him and will not refuse him, when they have agreed and nothing remains but the marriage contract. He should look at her only to acquaint himself with her state, not out of desire to look at her or to take pleasure in her, nor should he deliberately direct his gaze toward her private parts or toward what it is not fitting to look upon. It is not lawful for him to look with the eye of contemplation at women who are not his, that is, women other than his wives, those forbidden to him by blood, and those his right hand possesses, whether they be bareheaded or unveiled, for Allah says, exalted be He, ﴿قُل لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾, "Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze."

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), was asked about a man past whom a woman passes, and he looks at her from behind. He said: "Would it please one of you that men should look upon his womenfolk and his kinswomen? Be content for people with what you are content with for yourselves." And he said, (ع), concerning the saying of Allah Almighty in the story of Moses, recounting the words of the woman, ﴿قَالَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا يَا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ﴾, "One of the two women said: O my father, hire him; indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy," that she meant Moses, (ع) and his family. Her father said to her: "As for your saying that he is strong, that is from what you saw of his lifting the rock from the well; but how did you come to know his trustworthiness?" She said: "When he set out with me to come to you, I wished to walk before him to show him the road, but he came forward and said: Walk behind me and direct me to the road, for we are a people who do not look upon the backs of women."

It is narrated from Ali, (ع), that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, (ع), when looking at women was mentioned, and he said: "The first glance is for you," meaning the glance that falls unawares, "and the second is against you, and the third glance is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis. Whoever forsakes such glances for the sake of Allah Almighty, and for no other, Allah Almighty will requite him with a faith whose sweetness he will taste." And Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: "Do those who look upon the forms of women not fear that they may be afflicted with the like in their own wives?"

It is narrated from Ali, (ع), that a man came to the Messenger of Allah, (ع), and said: "O Messenger of Allah, should I ask my mother's leave before entering upon her?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah, (ع)?" He said: "Would it please you to see her unclothed?" He said: "No." He said: "Then ask her leave." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, (ع), my sister uncovers her hair before me." He said: "No." He said: "Why?" He said: "I fear that, should she reveal one of her charms before you, Satan may invite you toward her." And he said, (ع) and his family: "When one of you would kiss a woman who is a mahram to him and has come of age, a mother, a sister, an aunt, or any who is forbidden to him in marriage, let him kiss her upon the head and between the eyes, or let him refrain from her cheeks and her mouth."

Concerning Fatimah, (ع): a blind man sought leave to enter upon her, and she veiled herself from him. It was said to her: "He is blind, his sight is wholly gone; he sees nothing of her." She said: "Even if he does not see me, I see him, and he perceives the voice and senses the scent."

The Messenger of Allah, (ع), asked Ali, (ع), and a company that was before him, what is best for women, and they did not know what to say. Ali, (ع), withdrew to Fatimah, (ع), and mentioned this to her, and she said: "What is best for women is that they should not see men and that men should not see them." Ali, (ع), went to the Messenger of Allah, (ع), and said this to him. He said: "Did you arrive at this of yourself, or did another say it?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, (ع), it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah, (ع), was pleased by it and said: "Fatimah is but a part of me."

### The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice

The Messenger of Allah, (ع), taught that whoever desires to marry should not approach the matter heedlessly, but should begin by turning to Allah, praising Him and extolling Him, and then asking Him for the kind of companion that makes a household whole. He said that such a person should pray:

"O Allah, grant me a wife who is affectionate and fruitful, grateful and jealous in her honor. If I do good, she thanks me; if I do wrong, she forgives me; if I remember Allah, she helps me; if I forget, she reminds me; if I go out from her, she guards herself; if I come in to her, she gladdens me; if I command her, she obeys me; if I swear by her, she fulfills my oath; if she becomes angry, You satisfy me. O Lord of majesty and honor, grant me what I have asked for, and what You have apportioned and given."

And he made a clear promise concerning this supplication. The Messenger of Allah, (ع), said that whoever says these words and acts upon them, Allah Almighty will give him what he has asked.

He also taught that marriage is not a thing to be entered without its proper preliminaries. The Messenger of Allah, (ع), said that every marriage in which there is no engagement is like a leprous hand.

This same care for the right beginning was kept by his descendants. Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), when he gave a woman in marriage or when a marriage was contracted in his presence, would open with words of praise and witness, saying: "Praise be to Allah. We praise Him and seek refuge with Him from the evils of ourselves and the evils of our deeds. Whoever Allah guides, none can mislead, and whoever He leaves to stray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger."

Then he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا ﴾

And he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ ﴾

And he would recite the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا ۝ يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا ﴾

Once the marriage has been thus commended and the standing of each party made known to the other, the contract is concluded. The one who performs it praises Allah for what He deserves, prays upon the Prophet ((ع) and his family), recalls the virtue of marriage and what is desired in it, and only then ties the knot. It is fitting that the husband make known to his prospective companion whatever he can of his situation, so that she enters the union with knowledge of his circumstances. And if the contract is not preceded by a formal engagement, it remains permissible, though the khutbah is the better course.

The scholars (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) forbade a formal proposal during the iddah, yet they permitted a discreet hint at marriage, in keeping with the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا عَرَّضْتُم بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّا أَن تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوفًا ۚ وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْكِتَابُ أَجَلَهُ ﴾

*There is no blame upon you for what you hint at regarding a proposal to women, or what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will remember them, but do not make a secret commitment with them except in the form of honorable speech. And do not resolve the marriage contract until the prescribed term reaches its end.* (al-Baqarah: 235)

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, "do not make a secret commitment with them": this refers to a secret pledge of marriage, while exposing them gently to the matter and speaking goodly words is the permitted hinting at the khutbah.

It was narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that he entered upon Sakina bint Handhalah, who had been separated from a cousin of hers who had married her and then died. Abu Jafar greeted her and said, "How have you been, O daughter of Handhalah?" She said, "May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah." He said, "You know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family), and my standing with Ali (ع), and my right in Islam, and my honor among the Arabs." She said, "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Jafar. You propose to me while I am in my iddah!" He said, "I have done no such thing. I have only informed you of my status and my standing. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) once entered upon Umm Salamah, the daughter of Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumiyyah, while she was in her iddah from Abu Salamah, who was her cousin. He continued to mention his standing to her until the impression of the mat showed upon his palm from the force with which he leaned upon his hand, and yet that was not a formal proposal." They said (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ): it is recommended for one who wishes to marry to acquaint his prospective companion with his situation, so that she may know his circumstances.

It was related that when the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) proposed to her, Umm Salamah (رض) sent word to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I am an elderly woman, I have children, and I am a woman of great jealousy, and I fear there may be something in me of which you are unaware."
