The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent back to her, "As for your age, you have mentioned it, and I am older than you. As for your children, they shall be among the children of the Messenger of Allah. And as for your jealousy, I shall pray to Allah Almighty to remove it from you." And he married her ((ع) and his family).

**The Wedding Feast and the Consummation of Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah (may the prayers of Allah be upon him and upon his family and upon them all) that the feast is of four kinds: the walimah, the khurs, the idhar, and the wakirah. The walimah is the food prepared when a man enters upon his wife. The khurs is the food of the aqiqah prepared for the newborn on the seventh day, which has already been mentioned along with what is obligatory in it. The idhar is the food prepared at the circumcision of a boy. The wakirah is when a man returns from a journey, prepares food, and invites people to it. He said ((ع) and his family): it is among the Sunnah of the Messengers to provide food upon marriage. The Prophet ((ع) and his family) held a wedding feast for his wives when he consummated marriage with them, and at some of his feasts he served al-hays, a food made of dates, ghee, and condensed milk. He said (ع) to one of his companions who had married, "Give a feast, even if it be only with a sheep." And he said ((ع) and his family), "The feast of the first day is a duty, the feast of the second day is a kindness known among people, and what is beyond that is ostentation and reputation-seeking." Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (may the prayers of Allah be upon them) was invited to a feast on the first day and he answered it; he was invited on the second day and he answered it; then a messenger came to him on the third day to invite him, and he ordered the messenger turned away until he was out of sight.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he passed by Banu Zurayq and heard the sound of instruments and singing, and he asked, "What is this?" They said, "O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so has married so-and-so." He said, "He has completed his religion. This is marriage, not a clandestine affair, and there is no marriage in secret, until its smoke is seen and the sound of the tambourine is heard." And he said ((ع) and his family), "What distinguishes marriage from fornication is the beating of the tambourine." It was also narrated from him ((ع) and his family) that on the night Fatimah was brought to Ali (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) he heard the beat of the tambourine, and he asked, "What is this?" Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is Asma bint Umays beating the tambourine for Fatimah, lest she say within herself, My mother has died and there is no one to rejoice with me." The Messenger of Allah raised his hands to the heavens and said, "O Allah, bring joy to Asma bint Umays as she has gladdened the daughter of Your Prophet." Then he called her and said, "O Asma, what do you say when you beat the tambourine?" She said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah I do not know what to say; I only wished to gladden her." He said, "Then do not say anything indecent, but say: We have come to you, we have come to you; so greet us and we will greet you."

This kind of speech and its like, together with the beating of the tambourine and what resembles it, is what permission has been granted for at weddings and banquets. As for other speech that carries vulgarity, and the singing that accompanies it, and the instruments of diversion and the entrancing flutes that the people of frivolity take up, that is disliked.

Al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) was asked about such things, and he recited the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ ۝ لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَّاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ ۝ بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ ۚ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ ﴾

*We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play. Had We intended to take a pastime, We would have taken it from near Us, were We to do so. Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and at once it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.* (al-Anbiya: 16–18)

It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing is a gathering upon which Allah Almighty does not look." It was narrated from him that he was asked about the flute, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: there are two voices that Allah Almighty detests: a wailing at the time of calamity, and a flute at the time of blessing." And it was narrated from him regarding the words of Allah Almighty:

﴿ فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ وَاجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ ﴾

*So avoid the abomination of idols, and avoid the false statement* (al-Hajj: 30)

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

that "the abomination of idols" includes chess, and that "the false statement" includes singing. He said concerning the words of Allah Almighty, ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6), that this too refers to singing.

One of his companions said, "I was in Madinah and came upon a place where there was singing, so I sat and listened. The next day I entered upon Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), and when I sat before him he began by reciting the words of Allah, exalted be His mention:

﴿ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا ﴾

*Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart: about all those one will be questioned.* (al-Isra: 36)

Then he looked at me and said, You will be asked of your hearing what it heard, of your heart what it understood, and of your sight what it beheld."

It was narrated from him that he said, "The sale of singing is not lawful, nor its purchase; listening to it is hypocrisy, and teaching it is disbelief." It was also narrated from him that one day some of his Shia, who had come as a delegation from various towns, entered upon him, and he asked them, "Where have you lodged?" They said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, we lodged in a house, and when we drew near to the place we heard singing within it, so we sought another lodging but could not find one." He said, "Even so, be noble: keep your hearing far from listening to it and lending it your ear, for Allah, exalted is the One who speaks, says:

﴿ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا ﴾

*And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity.* (al-Furqan: 72)"

It was narrated from him that he said, "My father (ع) passed by me one day when I was a boy, and I had stopped to listen to two pipers. He took me by the hand and said, Step away; do not be of those who gloated over Adam (ع). I said, How is that, O my father? He said, All the amusement, play, and singing that you see was devised by Iblis to gloat over Adam (ع) when he was expelled from Paradise." He said (ع), "The house in which singing takes place is a house in which no calamity is met with comfort, no supplication is answered, and the angel does not enter." It was narrated from him that he said, "Singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart as water causes the date palm to bring forth its spathe." And it was narrated from him that he said, "Whoever has the lute played in his house for forty days, Allah sets over him a devil called al-Anqad, who leaves no limb of his without sitting upon it; and when he is thus afflicted, his sense of shame is stripped from him, and he no longer cares what he says or what is said to him."

> وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِى لَهْوَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ

It was mentioned to him (ع) that a man of his Shia had entered upon someone he knew, and that man brought out a slave-girl of his who played and sang, and she sang and played before him. Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said, "Did he not fear that the command of Allah Almighty might come upon him while he was in such a state, in a gathering upon which Allah does not look?" It was also narrated from him that a man asked him about singing, and he said to him, "Tell me: if Allah Almighty separates truth from falsehood, where do you see singing falling?" The man said, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, I see it only with falsehood." He said, "Then I reckon you have judged it. Leave it, for there is no good in it, and it is among that for which Allah Almighty has promised the Fire." Then he recited the words of Allah Almighty, ﴿ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ ﴾ *And among the people is he who purchases idle talk* (Luqman: 6). It was also narrated from him that singing bequeaths hypocrisy and brings on poverty.

And he said (ع) that the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade his community al-zafn, the flute, the drums, and the reed-pipes; and that a man who had broken a lute was once brought before Ali (ع), and Ali approved his deed and ruled that there was no liability for breaking the lute. All of this points to the prohibition of frivolity and of listening to singing, flutes, lyres, and the like that are taken up for diversion. As for what is used in war, in the marshaling and parading of troops, and the like, such as what people raise up before the Imams and the commanders of armies by beating drums and shields and by blowing horns and pipes that are not taken for enjoyment and amusement, that is not among what was forbidden, nor of the kind whose prohibition has just been mentioned. Rather it is among what is recommended in its proper place. For it has come from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he passed by a company of Abyssinians beating their drums, and he said, "Carry on, O sons of Arfidah, that the Jews may know there is breadth in our religion."

If someone should ask, "Why then do we hear and see, in the lands where the Imams hold authority (may the prayers of Allah be upon them), the very instruments of diversion that they have forbidden?" the answer is that this is no greater than the indecencies that Allah Almighty has forbidden and made unlawful, which people nonetheless commit in their homes, behind their doors and their curtains. Allah has commanded that the prescribed penalties be carried out for those indecencies upon which He has commanded such penalties, in what appears openly and is witnessed by witnesses. As for what remains hidden, He alone, glorified be He, holds the knowledge of it and has reserved to Himself both its punishment and its pardon, advancing of that what He wills and deferring what He defers. It is well known and widely established among all people that the Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) denounced these things upon those who did them and withheld any license for them, holding that this is not a matter for which the hadd is due, but rather one calling for denunciation and prohibition.

It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he said, "Bring your brides in by night, and give the feast by day." And it was narrated from him (ع) that he said, "There is no staying awake save in three: a vigil with the Quran, the seeking of knowledge, or the bringing of a bride to her husband." It was also narrated from him (ع) that a man should make himself ready for his wife as he would wish her to make herself ready for him; Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said that this means cleanliness.

He said: when a man's wife is brought to him and she enters upon him, let him pray two rakahs, then place his hand upon her forelock and say, "O Allah, bless me in my wife and bless her in me; in whatever You have joined between us, join us in goodness, felicity, and blessing; and if You decree a parting, make it a parting toward every good." Then, when he sits beside her, let him wipe her forelock and say, "Praise be to Allah, who guided my straying, enriched my poverty, raised up my burden, gave might to my lowliness, sheltered my dependents, gave a spouse to my solitude, bore up my step, served my need, brought company to my loneliness, and lifted my standing; a praise wholesome, abundant, and blessed, for what You have granted, O Lord, and for what You have apportioned, and for what You have honored."

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said: the woman too is commanded to be in a state of ablution on the night she is brought as a bride; when her husband prays, she prays, and when he supplicates, she says amen. He added that one should increase in supplication, sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) at the beginning, the middle, and the end, and saying within it, "O Allah, grant me her affection, her warmth, her contentment with me and my contentment with her, and join us in the best of unions and the gentlest of bonds, for You love the lawful and hate the unlawful."

And Jafar ibn Muhammad (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said: when a man wishes to come to his wife, let him say, "O Allah, if You decree from me this day a child, then make him purely Yours, and grant the devil no share in him, no portion and no part; indeed You are powerful over all things." It was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he said, "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her," and that when he is with her, let him deal kindly and truly with her. And he ((ع) and his family) forbade that a man be intimate with a free woman while another woman is in the room with her. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said there is no harm in that with a bondwoman, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع). And it was narrated from Ali (ع) that he said it does not befit a man to be intimate with his wife

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), said that when a man wishes to come to his wife, let him say: «اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ قَضَيْتَ مِنِّي الْيَوْمَ خَلْقًا فَاجْعَلْهُ لَكَ خَالِصًا، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ لِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ شِرْكًا وَلَا حَظًّا وَلَا نَصِيبًا، إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» "O Allah, if You decree from me today a creation, make it purely for You, and grant the devil in it no share, no portion, and no part, for You are able to do all things." And from the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, it was related that he said: «إِذَا أَتَىٰ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَلَا يُعْجِلْهَا، وَإِذَا وَاقَعَهَا فَلْيَصْدُقْهَا» "When one of you comes to his wife, let him not hasten her, and when he is with her, let him deal truthfully with her."

He, (ع) and his family, permitted a man to come to a free wife while another wife is present in the house. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said there is no objection to this in the case of a bondwoman, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع). From Ali, (ع), it was related that a man should not come to his wife while facing the qibla. He also said that to gaze during intercourse brings on blindness. The Prophet, (ع) and his family, and the Imams of his progeny, would turn the face away from any animal being mounted upon the road, and he would avert his face, (ع).

He, (ع), named a hidden form of infanticide, الْوَأْدُ الْخَفِيُّ: that a man comes to a woman, and when he senses the issuing of the fluid he withdraws from her and spills it elsewhere. Of this he said, "So do not do that." He said that the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, forbade withdrawal from a free woman except with her leave, and from a bondwoman taken in marriage except with the leave of her master. Ali, (ع), said that a man may withdraw from his own bondwoman as he wishes, and likewise said Jafar ibn Muhammad, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ).

From Ali, (ع), by way of Jafar ibn Muhammad: a man should not lie between two free women, though he may lie between two bondwomen; and he should not look upon the awrah of a free woman, nor expose his own awrah to her. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said that intercourse is disliked from the breaking of dawn until sunrise, and from the setting of the sun until the fading of twilight; and on the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed; and on the day and night in which the earth quakes; and when the yellow, the black, and the red winds blow.

He, (ع), said: The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, passed a night with one of his wives on a night in which the moon was eclipsed, and nothing passed between him and her. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is this coldness?" He said, "It is no coldness, but this was a sign, and I was loath to take my pleasure on such a night, that I might not be among those whom Allah, mighty and majestic, has rebuked in His Book where He says: «وَإِن يَرَوْا كِسْفًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ» And were they to see a fragment falling from the sky, they would say: a heaped-up cloud." Then Abu Jafar, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: By Him who sent Muhammad with prophethood, singled him out with the message, and honored him with nobility, none of you comes to his wife at any of these disliked times and is then granted offspring in whom he sees the delight of his eye.

From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him: a slave girl under nine years of age is not to be approached; if a man does so and she is harmed by it, he is liable. Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, said: If a man marries a young girl, he does not enter upon her until she completes nine years from the day of her birth.

From Ali, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, it was related that he disliked the coming to women in their hinder parts, and he used to forbid it, citing the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, that one may come to them only «فِي الْفُرُوجِ مِنْ قُبُلٍ أَوْ دُبُرٍ» in the place of tilth, whether from before or from behind. And from the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, it was related that he said: «لَا يَخْلُو رَجُلٌ بِامْرَأَةٍ غَيْرِ ذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ مِنْهُ إِلَّا كَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ ثَالِثَهُمَا» "No man is alone with a woman who is not his mahram but that the devil is the third of them." He forbade conversing with women other than one's wives and one's mahrams. Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: «حَدِيثُ النِّسَاءِ يُورِثُ النِّسْيَانَ وَيُزِيغُ الْقَلْبَ وَهُوَ مِنْ مَصَائِدِ الشَّيْطَانِ» "Idle talk with women breeds forgetfulness and makes the heart swerve, and it is among the snares of the devil."

> فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَىْءٍۢ مِّنْهُ

The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, said: «اِتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي النِّسَاءِ، فَإِنَّهُنَّ عِيٌّ وَعَوْرَةٌ، وَإِنَّكُمُ اسْتَحْلَلْتُمُوهُنَّ بِأَمَانَةِ اللَّهِ» "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are weak of speech and are a thing to be covered, and you have made them lawful to you by the trust of Allah." He said: They have their weakness, so treat their weakness with restraint of speech, and shelter that which is to be covered within the homes; do not lodge them in the upper rooms, do not teach them to write, but teach them Surat al-Nur. And from him, (ع) and his family, he said: «نِعْمَ شُغْلُ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُؤْمِنَةِ الْمِغْزَلُ» "How excellent an occupation for a believing woman is the spindle." From him also, (ع) and his family, when he took the pledge from women he would take upon them that they would not speak with men other than their husbands and their mahrams.

It was related from him, (ع) and his family, that he forbade women to look upon men, and that a woman should not leave her house without her husband's leave, not even for the bath save out of necessity. And it was related that he said one day to his companions, "What is the woman?" They said, "An awrah, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Yes." Then he said, "And when is she nearest to her Lord?" They had no answer to give. Ali mentioned this to Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, and she said, "Return to him and say: O Messenger of Allah, the nearest a woman is to her Lord is when she keeps to the innermost of her house." He went and informed the Prophet, (ع) and his family, who said, "This is from you, O Ali." He said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, rather it was Fatimah who said it." The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, said, "She has spoken truly; «إِنَّهَا بِضْعَةٌ مِنِّي» indeed she is a part of me."

From the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family: he forbade a woman to walk unclothed before her husband, and forbade the man to be unclothed before her. He forbade women to comb their hair with wine or to apply its dregs, and he forbade women to imitate men and men to imitate women, and he cursed whoever did so. From him, (ع): "Any woman who perfumes herself, let her not leave her house, nor attend the prayer with us." And from him: he forbade women, when they go out behind men, to walk in the middle of the road with them, and he said, "Women have no portion of the middle of the road." He forbade, (ع), that a woman should wear, when she goes out, a garment that draws notice, or adorn herself with what makes a sound, or strike with her foot so that the chime of her anklet is heard. He forbade women from open display, from wailing, and from raising the voice except out of necessity, and from conversing with men, and from passing the night away from their homes.

He forbade, (ع), the giving of greeting to women. And from him, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said that a man should not touch a man unless there is a garment between them, nor a woman a woman unless there is a garment between them. From him, (ع) and his family: a woman came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a husband who is harsh of nature, and I have worked something to turn his affection toward me." The Messenger of Allah, (ع), said to her, "Fie upon you! You have sullied your religion, and the angels of heaven and the angels of earth have cursed you." From him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: «لَوْ كُنْتُ آمِرًا أَحَدًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِأَحَدٍ لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا» "Had I been commanding anyone to prostrate to another, I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband." He forbade a woman to deny her husband herself when he called her, and to deny him her help and her work. He said, "The best thing with which a woman adorns herself is the fear of Allah and obedience to her husband."

He said, (ع) and his family: When a woman knows her Lord and believes in Him and in His Messenger, and acknowledges the merit of the People of the House of her Prophet, and prays the five prayers, and fasts the month of Ramadan, and guards her chastity, and obeys her husband, she enters by whichever of the gates of Paradise she wishes. From him, (ع): a woman sent to him saying, "O Messenger of Allah, my husband has ordered me not to go out, near or far, until he returns from his journey; and my father is in the market. Shall I go out to him?" The Messenger of Allah, (ع), said to her, "Sit in your house and obey your husband." So she did, and her father died. The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, sent to her saying, "Truly Allah, mighty and majestic, has forgiven your father on account of your obedience to your husband."

A woman asked him, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the husband over the wife?" He said, "She must not give in charity from his house except by his leave, nor deny him herself even upon the saddle's back, nor fast a voluntary day except by his leave, nor leave her house except by his leave; and if she goes out without his leave, the angels of heaven, the angels of earth, the angels of mercy, and the angels of wrath curse her until she returns." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, who has the greatest right over a man?" He said, "His parents." "And who has the greatest right over a woman?" He said, "Her husband." She said, "O Messenger of Allah, then have I no right over him to match what he has over me?" He said, "No, not even one in a hundred." And it was related that he, (ع), assigned to his daughter Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, the service of what was within the house, and assigned to Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, the service of what was outside it.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon him, was asked about the right of the woman over her husband, the fulfilling of which makes him a doer of good. He said: He feeds her and clothes her, and when she wrongs him he pardons her. He said: My father, may Allah's blessings be upon him, had a wife who used to vex him, and he would forgive her and would say: The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, said: «اَلْمَرْأَةُ كَالضِّلَعِ، إِنْ تَرَكْتَهَا اِنْتَفَعْتَ بِهَا، وَإِنْ أَقَمْتَهَا كَسَرْتَهَا» "The woman is like a rib: if you leave it be, you take benefit from it, and if you try to straighten it, you break it." It was said to him, "But the woman is jealous over her husband." He said, "That is love."

He was asked, (ع), about a man who turns away from his wife because worship, fasting, and prayer occupy him from her. He said: The wife of Uthman ibn Mazun came to the Messenger of Allah, (ع), and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Uthman fasts the day and stands the night in prayer." He understood, (ع) and his family, what she intended, and he went out to the mosque, where he found Uthman ibn Mazun standing in prayer, and he said, "O Uthman, Allah, mighty and majestic, did not send me with monasticism; He sent me with the upright way. Whoever loves my nature, let him follow my Sunnah, and among my Sunnah is marriage." And the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, forbade the striking of women where it is not warranted.

From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him: a man of the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, with his daughter and said, "O Messenger of Allah, her husband has struck her; grant her retaliation against him." The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, granted her that. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down: «الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ وَبِمَا أَنفَقُوا مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ ۚ فَالصَّالِحَاتُ قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ لِّلْغَيْبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهُ ۚ وَاللَّاتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ ۖ فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ فَلَا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا» "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has favored some of them over others, and because they spend of their wealth. So the righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard. As for those from whom you fear discord, admonish them, then leave them apart in their beds, then strike them. But if they obey you, seek no way against them. Surely Allah is Most High, Most Great." (al-Nisa: 34) And the Messenger of Allah, (ع), then said: «أَرَدْتُ أَمْرًا وَأَرَادَ اللَّهُ غَيْرَهُ» "I intended one thing, and Allah intended another."

From him, (ع), he said that jealousy is a part of faith, and a careless yielding is a part of hypocrisy, meaning jealousy in what is forbidden, and the yielding that brings men and women together for that. In another report from Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, forbade al-madhal, which is the abandonment of due jealousy. Its root is from a man's making known his secret, that is, exposing it, and from this is taken a man's exposing of his womenfolk to other men. As for jealousy in what is lawful, it is disliked and forbidden. Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, said: There is no jealousy in the lawful, in light of the saying of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, on the night he brought Fatimah, may Allah's blessings be upon her, in to her husband, after she had come to be his: «لَا تُحْدِثَا شَيْئًا حَتَّىٰ آتِيَكُمَا» "Do not do anything until I come to you." He said this to them after they had lain down. So Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, held back, and the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, entered and prayed for them and blessed them, and then departed.

From the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, he said: «كُتِبَ الْجِهَادُ عَلَىٰ رِجَالِ أُمَّتِي وَالْغَيْرَةُ عَلَىٰ نِسَائِهَا، فَمَنْ صَبَرَتْ مِنْهُنَّ وَاحْتَسَبَتْ أَعْطَاهَا اللَّهُ أَجْرَ شَهِيدٍ» "Striving has been prescribed upon the men of my community, and jealousy upon its women; so whichever of them is patient and seeks her reward, Allah, mighty and majestic, grants her the reward of a martyr." From him, (ع), he mentioned women and what they ask of men, and said: They burden men, when they deck themselves in gold and wear silk; they burden the rich and wear out the poor. And from Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: Whoever obeys his wife in four things, Allah casts him upon his face into the Fire: that he obey her in going to wedding feasts, to gatherings of wailing, to visitings, and to the bathhouses.

**On Marriage Through Guardians**

We have related from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family: «لَا نِكَاحَ إِلَّا بِوَلِيٍّ وَشَاهِدَيْ عَدْلٍ» "There is no marriage save with a guardian and two upright witnesses." And he forbade that a woman be given in marriage until she is consulted. From Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: None of you should give his daughter in marriage until he consults her, for she knows best her own self; if she keeps silent, or weeps, or laughs, that is her leave, and if she refuses, he does not marry her off. The arranging by fathers of the marriage of their minor sons and daughters is permissible, and they have no right of dissolution when they come of age; and when an agent is authorized to contract a marriage, it is valid. From him, may Allah's blessings be upon him, he said: If a Muslim woman, being of age, authorizes her Christian father to give her in marriage, and he does so, the marriage is valid; but if he gives her in marriage while she is a child, it is not valid, for a disbeliever has no guardianship over a Muslim.

When a woman entrusts two guardians and delegates the matter to both of them, and each of them marries her to a different man, the marriage belongs to the first of the two, provided that the first was unaware of the other's contract. If the two contracts are concluded at one and the same time, one of them is annulled and the matter is begun anew thereafter. From Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), and from Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), it is related that they said: A paternal grandfather may contract the marriage of his son's minor daughter just as the father contracts it, and he has the prior right in this, even if the two of them should contract at the same moment. All of them are bound by the first contract concluded among them, even if the one whose contract is dissolved was unaware of the other and only learns of it afterward, in which case the matter is resumed.

From Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), it is related that he said: Whatever testimony is admissible in financial matters is admissible in marriage, and the testimony of women and of slaves is accepted in it. From Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع): He was asked about two witnesses who testified in the marriage of a woman that her father had given her in marriage while she was unwilling, and another witness testified that he had given her in marriage with her consent. He said: The marriage is valid with her consent. He was also asked about two witnesses, one of whom testified that the dowry was one thousand and the other that it was two thousand. He said: If she claims the greater amount, she takes an oath together with her witness, and it is decreed for her. If one of them testifies that her father gave her in marriage while she was a child, and the other testifies that he gave her in marriage when she was of age and without her consent, the testimony is void.

**Mentioning the Witnesses in Marriage**

I have mentioned in what came before this chapter that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: There is no marriage save with a guardian and two witnesses. This is what is commanded, and upon it action is taken, and by it the marriage is established. It is related from Ali, (ع), that he said: A marriage is not valid except with a guardian and witnesses. Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), said: Witnesses were appointed in marriage only for the sake of the child, so that it may be known who his father is, and as a safeguard against either of the spouses denying the marriage, and out of caution before the authorities, lest the two be charged with being a man and a woman united unlawfully. For this reason, and for whatever resembles it, the seeking of witnesses in marriage is obligatory. As for what lies between a person and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is nothing upon him if he does not call witnesses, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned witnessing only in the matter of divorce and did not mention it in the matter of marriage. Yet witnesses in marriage cannot be dispensed with, because through them the marriage is established, lineage is confirmed, and doubt is removed, and upright persons bear witness to it. Among the witnesses, women and slaves are admissible, provided they are upright.

**Mentioning the Dowries**

We narrate concerning the Commander of the Believers, (ع). Allah, exalted be the One who speaks, said: ﴿ وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً ﴾. Ali, (ع), said concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿ وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is saying, give them the gift by which you have made their private parts lawful to you. So whoever wrongs a woman in her dowry has made her private part lawful to himself through fornication. And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives every sin save the sin of a man who has defrauded a hired laborer of his wage, or a woman of her dowry, or who has sold a free person.

It is related from him, (ع), that he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, did not marry any of his wives, nor did he give any of his daughters in marriage, for more than twelve uqiyyahs and a nashsh of silver. An uqiyyah is forty dirhams, and a nashsh is half an uqiyyah, so that is five hundred dirhams in all, together with a woven cloak and a bed of ram's hide. This is the dowry of the Sunnah. There is no fixed limit set upon dowries, and whatever is named, be it little or much, the marriage is contracted upon it. It is recommended that it be made easy. Ali, (ع), said: Among the blessings of a woman is the ease of her marriage and the ease of her womb, so do not be excessive in the dowries of women, for that breeds enmity.

He, (ع), said: A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to marry a certain woman. He said: Do you have anything to give her? The man said: No, by Allah, I have nothing. So he looked at a ring upon his hand and said: This ring that is on your hand. The man said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Then you have married her with this ring of yours. So ease in marriage is a merit, as has been related, and there is no harm in going beyond it either. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿ وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا ﴾. And it has come down from al-Husayn ibn Ali, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) both, that he married a woman and sent to her one hundred slave girls, with each slave girl a thousand dirhams.

We have narrated from Abu Abdullah, (ع), that he was asked about the dowry, and he said: It is whatever the two spouses agree upon, be it little or much. But a dowry there must be, and no marriage is permissible without a dowry, though there is no harm in contracting it without one being named, and he may not consummate it until he gives her something, whatever it may be. This is for the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً ﴾. So a contract without a named dowry is, on this basis, permissible, but he may not consummate it until he gives her something. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), was asked about this and said: My father, (ع), married a woman and did not name a dowry for her, and when he wished to consummate the marriage he took a garment from me and handed it to her.

He, (ع), was asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ ﴾. He said: That is something singled out for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. No marriage is sound except with a dowry. If he does not name a dowry for her and then dies before her, or divorces her before consummating the marriage, she has no dowry, yet he inherits from her and she from him, and she must observe the waiting period. If he has consummated the marriage, she is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, according to her condition, her wealth, and her beauty, measured against one of his like in condition and in wealth, provided that this does not exceed the dowry of the Sunnah. If it does exceed it, the excess is returned to him, and the dowry of the Sunnah, as we have mentioned, is five hundred dirhams.

It is related from him, (ع), concerning a man who married a woman upon her own determination, that he said: The marriage is valid; and if the two disagree as to the amount of the dowry, she is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, neither falling short nor going to excess, and it is not permissible for it to exceed the dowry of the Sunnah.

It is related from him, (ع), that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, forbade the marriage of exchange. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: The marriage of exchange, shighar, is that a man give his daughter in marriage to another man on the condition that the other give him his daughter in marriage, with no dowry between them. He said: Two men came to Ali, (ع), and each married the other's daughter without a dowry, so he rejected it and said: No, there must be a dowry. This applies when the contract in such a marriage is made on the basis that the marriage of the one is in return for the marriage of the other, each being set as the recompense for the other, and they oblige themselves to this. But if they contract it as a marriage is contracted without a named dowry, and do not stipulate within it what we have described, then the contract is valid, and each of the two women is entitled to the like of the dowry of the women of her family, in the manner we have described.

They, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), permitted the contracting of marriage upon described and known goods. They narrated from Ali, (ع), that he said concerning a man who married a woman in return for a young servant: neither falling short nor going to excess. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: Whoever marries a woman for an unknown dowry has not thereby corrupted the marriage; she is entitled to the like of the dowry of her peers, and it shall be no more than the dowry of the Sunnah.

He, (ع), was asked about a man who married a woman in return for a slave girl of his who had been pledged her freedom upon his death, and who then divorced her before consummating the marriage. He said: The woman is entitled to half the service of the pledged slave girl, so that the woman has one day of her service and her master one day; and if the master revokes the pledge of freedom or sells her, the woman is entitled to half her value. They, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), said: The dowry belongs to the woman. They narrated from Ali, (ع), that he said: Marriage in return for a wage paid to the father is not lawful in Islam, in the manner that Moses hired himself out. The dowry belongs only to the wife. If a man marries a woman on the condition that he perform some work for her, the marriage is valid, and the wage in that case stands in place of the dowry; he may not consummate the marriage until he has done for her the work for which he was engaged, or has given her something.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and said: O Messenger of Allah, give me in marriage. He said: Who will take this woman? A man among the people said: I, O Messenger of Allah. He said: What will you give her? He said: I have no wealth. He said: With no wealth at all? So the woman turned to go. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, repeated his words, and no one rose but that man, and the woman turned away again. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to the man a third time: Do you know anything of the Quran? He said: Yes. He said: I have given her to you in marriage for what you know of the Quran. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: If a man marries a woman on the condition that he teach her a chapter from the Book of Allah, I would not have him consummate the marriage until he has taught her or given her something.

From Ali, (ع), it is related that he said: Once a woman has been brought in to her husband, she has no claim to her dowry after she has entered upon him except by clear proof, meaning, if she claims that he gave her nothing and that something of her dowry remains owing to her. Abu Abdullah Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: If he marries her with a portion paid at once and a portion deferred, the immediate portion falls due before consummation, and he may not consummate the marriage if she withholds herself from him until he pays it to her. The deferred portion runs until death or separation, that is, when no time of payment has been stipulated upon him. But if she stipulates that it become due after consummation, it has been related from Ali, (ع), that a woman brought before him a man who had married her, consummated the marriage, and named a term for her dowry, and Ali, (ع), said: There is no term for you in her dowry once you have consummated the marriage; her right has fallen due, so pay her her right. This, and Allah knows best, is when he had paid her nothing in advance, or had named for her neither an immediate nor a deferred portion. But if he named that and paid her at once what he had obligated upon himself, then the deferred remainder runs to the time he stipulated, for the words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: People are bound by their conditions. Likewise, if he named no term but named a dowry for her, and she refused that he consummate the marriage until he discharge it, that is her right.

From Ali, (ع), it is related that he said concerning a man who marries a woman and witnesses are called secretly the first time upon one dowry and openly another time upon a greater dowry: the first is the marriage contract, and by it the matter is taken. From him, (ع), that he said: When the curtains are let down and the doors are shut, the dowry has fallen due. This is the saying of Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), and that is when the woman claims that the union took place. But if she acknowledges that he did not touch her, even though he had let down his curtain and shut his door upon them, and he then divorces her, she is entitled to no more than half the dowry, and she must observe the waiting period, for the waiting period is not waived from her by her claim that he did not touch her once he has shut his door and let down his curtain over her.

From Ali and Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), it is related that they said concerning a man who makes the freeing of his slave woman her dowry: that this is permissible. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali, (ع), said: That is when the condition is set before the freeing, that is, he says: I marry you on the condition that I have made your dowry your freedom, and then he frees her. But if he frees her first and says to her: I free you for the sake of Allah on the condition that your freedom is your dowry and I marry you upon that, then the choice is hers: if she wishes she marries him, and if she wishes she does not, because she has been freed and has come to own herself apart from him. If he marries her after that, let him marry her with a dowry.

From Ali, (ع), it is related that he was asked about a man who steals wealth and marries with it, or buys a slave girl with it. He said: The union is lawful, but the liability for the wealth remains upon him, and he is a sinner for what he has done, and he must make restitution for what he stole.

**Mentioning the Conditions in Marriage**

We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and from the Imams of his household, that he said: Every condition that contradicts the Book of Allah is to be rejected. From Ali, (ع), it is related that he ruled concerning a man who married a woman and stipulated to her family that if he were to take another wife over her she would be divorced, or if he were to take a concubine over her the concubine would be free. He said: The condition of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, comes before their conditions. If he wishes, he fulfills his promise; and if he wishes, he marries another over her or takes a concubine, and no wife is divorced from him should he marry her, nor is any concubine freed should he take her. From Abu Jafar and Abu Abdullah, (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), the like of this is related.

It was narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), as likewise from Ali (ع), that he gave judgment concerning a man who married a woman and stipulated that she should hold authority over her own affairs. Ali said: This departs from the Sunnah and assigns a right to one who is not its rightful holder. The husband is the guardian; intimacy and divorce rest in his hand. He therefore ruled that the dowry was owed by the husband, that intimacy and divorce remained his, and he nullified the condition.

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: A condition that is lawful, one that does not contradict the Book of Allah, is binding upon the man who married the woman on its basis. Among such valid conditions is that she shall remain with her family in a known land, or in a specified dwelling. This is permissible.

It was also narrated from him (ع) that he said: Whoever marries a woman on the condition that he will provide her a fixed daily maintenance and not be absent from her during the day, that condition does not invalidate the marriage, but neither is it itself binding; she retains the right to the division of nights and to the maintenance due to wives generally. Yet if a man marries a woman who fears that he may harm her or divorce her, and he agrees with her to forgo some of his rights regarding her maintenance and the division of nights, that is permissible, in accordance with the words of Allah the Almighty: "If a woman fears discord or desertion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they come to an agreement between themselves" (al-Nisa 128).

Abu Abd-Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: If he stipulates for her that, should he take another wife or take a concubine, she shall have one hundred dinars or whatever sum he has bound himself to, the marriage is permissible. If the sum he has committed is drawn from the original dowry, it is binding; if it rests only upon the added stipulation, it is not binding. This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع): A man should not make the divorce of one wife a condition for marrying another. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade a woman to seek the divorce of her sister wife so that she might take her place, for Allah the Almighty is the One who provides for her. And the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade the marriage of pleasure (mutah).

Concerning the marriage of pleasure which some had allowed: it is reported that a man would say to a woman, "Give yourself to me in marriage," and would say, "I marry you for this dirham," or two dirhams, or whatever sum was named, for a single union, or a day, or two days, or whatever term they agreed upon. They said that once they agreed on this it became permissible for him until the end of the agreed term; and when the term expired the separation occurred of itself, without divorce. They claimed there was no iddah upon her, that she did not inherit from him nor he from her, and that intimacy by this arrangement was not permissible with a virgin, though some of them claimed it was permissible even with women already married. This is pure fornication, in which there is no ambiguity and which admits of no covering. Allah the Almighty has permitted intimacy only through two paths, through the bond of marriage and through the right hand of possession (milk al-yamin), for the Almighty said: "Those who guard their private parts, except with their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy; but whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors" (al-Muminun 5–7).

> يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحْصُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ

For if this pleasure union were a marriage, the woman could not be parted from the man without divorce and without iddah, since Allah the Almighty says: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period" (al-Talaq 1); and she would inherit and be inherited from, since Allah says: "And you shall have half of what your wives leave" (al-Nisa 12), and "They shall have a fourth of what you leave" (al-Nisa 12); and the child would be attached to them both, for the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said: "The child belongs to the bed," meaning to the owner of the bed. But in this arrangement there is neither marriage nor right of possession, and what remains is forbidden. The reports forbidding the marriage of pleasure from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) are many, as is his saying, "There is no marriage except with a guardian and two upright witnesses." Those who uphold the marriage of pleasure themselves claim that it is contracted without a guardian and without witnesses, and so it cannot stand. It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that they declared the marriage of pleasure void, forbade it, and prohibited it.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he gave judgment concerning a slave-woman who had fled from her master and deceived a man by claiming to be free, so that he married her on that basis and she bore him children; then her master established his claim over her. He ruled that she be returned to her master, and that the man who had been deceived owed her master the value of his children by her, unless the master chose to grant the children to their father. If the man had bought her and she bore him a child, and her master then established his claim, she was to be returned to the one whose right was vindicated, and the value of the child was owed by the father, who could in turn recover it from the one who had sold her to him. But if he had taken her by force, or had known when he married her that she was owned and that her master had not given her in marriage, then both she and her child belonged to the master.

From Ali (ع) it was narrated concerning a free woman whom a male slave had approached, claiming to be free, so that she married him on that basis and then learned that he was owned: they may be separated if the woman wishes. Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) said: She holds authority over her own decision; if she wishes she may remain with him, and if she wishes she may leave him. If she chooses to separate and the marriage has not been consummated, she is owed nothing; but if it has been consummated, she is entitled to her dowry, and the liability falls upon whoever deceived her, whether the slave himself or another. When the slave is freed, if his lord does not give him in marriage to her, the dowry rests with the slave once he is free; and if the lord gave him in marriage, or gave him leave to marry her, then her dowry is owed by the lord.

It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) concerning a man to whom another woman was brought as a bride, so that he consummated the marriage believing her to be his wife and only afterward learned otherwise: he must return that woman, and she is entitled to a dowry for what was done to her, claimed against the one who deceived him, and his true wife, the one he had actually married, is to be restored to him.

It was narrated from them concerning a man who is impotent and unable to approach women, yet conceals this from the woman he marries: she has the right of choice once she comes to know, and she is entitled to the dowry if she exercises that choice and the marriage has been consummated. They also said concerning a man who marries a woman and finds in her leprosy, or vitiligo, or blindness, or insanity, or a condition in the private parts that prevents intercourse, or a manifest lameness: the husband has the right of choice; if he wishes he may keep her, and if he wishes he may return her. She is entitled to the dowry if he has had intercourse with her, and his claim for it is against the one who deceived him with her, while the woman herself owes nothing in return. For defects other than these she is not to be returned.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) concerning a man who marries a woman as a virgin and finds her otherwise: he saw nothing objectionable in this, and said that virginity may be lost through a leap, through ablution, or through the passing of long years.

Mentioning the Forbidden Marriage and the Permissible Marriage

Allah the Almighty said: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed; it is an indecency and a hateful thing and an evil way. Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters..." (al-Nisa 22–23). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has thus forbidden in the plain text of His Book the marriage of those He named explicitly, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Imams of his house (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) made clear what required clarification.

> وَرَبَٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّتِى فِى حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّتِى دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ

It came from Ali and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) concerning the mention of the mothers of wives that the matter is unrestricted: when a man marries a woman, her mother becomes forbidden to him, whether or not he has consummated the marriage with the daughter. They said: if a man marries a woman and then divorces her, or she dies before he has consummated the marriage, the marriage of her daughter remains lawful for him, in keeping with the words of Allah: "And your stepdaughters under your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage; but if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you" (al-Nisa 23). The "guardianship" here is the bond of inviolability. But if he has consummated the marriage with the woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him; and likewise, if he has seen of her what is forbidden to other men, he may not marry her daughter.

It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) concerning a man who marries a woman and then dies leaving her, or divorces her before consummation: she is forbidden to his son for all the generations that descend, and to his fathers however far they ascend. And if a man looks upon his bondswoman with desire, or touches her, or looks upon her nakedness, she becomes forbidden to his sons and to his fathers. But if one of them owned her and did not approach her, nor touch her, nor look upon her with desire, and then the other came to own her, she is lawful to him. They permitted the owning of two sisters together, while forbidding their combination in marriage. They said: if a man has approached one of the two, the other becomes forbidden to him, and he may not approach the second until the first has left his ownership through manumission, sale, or gift; and it does not suffice for him to give her to his son. If she dies, the other becomes lawful to him; what is forbidden is only their combination in marriage, for Allah says: "And that you combine two sisters" (al-Nisa 23), making no exception there between the owned woman and the free.

It was narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd-Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that a man should not marry the sister of a woman he has divorced until her iddah has elapsed and his right of revocation over her is extinguished; for so long as that right remains, he has effectively joined the two sisters together. But if the divorce was a final and irrevocable one, he may marry her sister, or another, provided he has no more than three other free wives besides her. They also said that a woman may not be joined with her paternal aunt, nor with her maternal aunt. Ali (ع) said: The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) forbade that, and made it unlawful. The daughter of Hamza was offered to him in marriage, and he said: Do you not know that she is the daughter of my brother through suckling, for I was nursed together with Hamza.

They (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) saw no harm in joining the daughters of paternal uncles with the daughters of maternal uncles, nor in a man's marrying both his wife and a daughter of his by another. Likewise, when a man divorces a woman or dies and another man marries her thereafter, there is no harm in the son of her first husband, by another wife, marrying the daughter of her second husband by another wife. They said: if a man commits fornication with the mother of his wife, or her sister, or her daughter, this does not corrupt his marriage, for the unlawful does not corrupt the lawful. But if he commits fornication with a woman and she then bears a child, it is not proper for his son by another wife to marry that woman's daughter. They granted permission regarding the woman with whom a man had committed fornication once both have repented.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) concerning a woman who commits adultery before her husband has consummated the marriage with her: they are separated, she is owed no dowry, and the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out upon her. Her dowry is forfeited because the offense arose from her side. Yet the separation rests upon the husband's wish: if he holds to her, she remains his wife.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع), when asked about a sick man who contracts a marriage and then dies, said: the marriage is valid, and she inherits from him.

It was narrated from Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) concerning a man who marries two sisters, or five women, in a single marriage contract: the one whose name was mentioned first among the sisters at the time of the contract has a valid marriage, and four of the five women have valid marriages, while the marriage of the second sister, and of the fifth woman after the four, is annulled. If it cannot be known which was named first, the whole contract is void. They (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said concerning a man who marries a woman during her iddah, or marries her while one of the two is in a state of consecration, both knowing that this is not lawful: they are separated, and she is never again lawful to him. But if they were ignorant, they are separated, and they may contract anew once she becomes lawful to suitors.

Mentioning the Missing Husband

We have narrated from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) that he said: if a man is reported dead to his family, so that his wife observes her iddah and then remarries, and afterward the first husband returns, the first husband has the greater right to her, whether or not the second husband has consummated the marriage. If the second husband has consummated it, she is entitled to her dowry for what was made lawful from her.

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: the wife of the missing man is to be left in her state so long as she keeps silent. But if she brings her case before the governor, he sets for her a term of four years and writes to inquire after her husband. If four years pass and no news of him comes, the governor summons the guardian of the missing man and asks whether the missing man has wealth. If he has wealth from which she may be maintained, and the guardian spends upon her from it, or the guardian spends upon her from his own means, then she has no way to remarry. But if the guardian will not maintain her and the missing man has no wealth, the governor compels the guardian to divorce her with a single pronouncement at the onset of her iddah while she is in a state of purity, and the guardian's divorce stands as the husband's divorce. If her husband returns before her iddah is complete, he has the greater right to her; and if her iddah has ended, she is lawful to suitors.

It was said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family), what is to be done if the guardian provides for her and she says, "I cannot be patient; I want what other women have"? He answered that she has no such recourse, and no claim to it, so long as the guardian provides for her.

The missing man (al-mafqud) is one who has departed his home and whose whereabouts are unknown. He may have been seen between the two battle lines in time of war, after which the people scattered and he was lost; or he may have set sail on a ship that capsized; or it may simply be that no one on the journey knows where he settled. As for a man whose location is known, his ruling is not that of the missing man. The ruling concerning his wife is that of a woman whose husband is merely absent (ghaib): she may not remarry unless he dies or divorces her. He (ع) said: if the whereabouts of the absent man are known, his wife may not remarry.

On Breastfeeding (al-Rida)

> وَرَبَٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّتِى فِى حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّتِى دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ

I have mentioned above the saying of Allah Almighty: ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُم مِّنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ﴾, "and your mothers who have suckled you, and your sisters through breastfeeding." We have narrated from the Imams of the family of the Messenger of Allah ((ع), and (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ)) that what is forbidden through lineage is forbidden through breastfeeding. I have already set out which of the women are forbidden in marriage, and whoever comes, through breastfeeding, to occupy the place of one of these holds the same status of prohibition.

It is permissible for a man to marry a woman who has breastfed his sons, and to marry from among her daughters those she did not nurse him alongside, because she is not his mother through breastfeeding and is not a wife to his father. He may likewise marry her daughter when the woman is among the daughters of a woman who breastfed his brother or his sister. In the same way, a man may marry the daughters of women who breastfed his son, and their daughters, for they did not nurse his son, and there is no bond between them and him, whether through breastfeeding or otherwise. What is forbidden is to marry the nursing woman herself; but the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts, and of maternal uncles and aunts, through breastfeeding are lawful to marry, just as they are lawful through lineage. A man may marry a woman while his father marries her daughter by another man, and a father and son may each marry one of two sisters.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he said: breastfeeding makes forbidden whether it be little or much; even a single suckle creates prohibition, by the saying of Allah Almighty, ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ﴾, "and your mothers who have suckled you." Breastfeeding applies to the little and the much alike, for even a small quantity nourishes, and from it flesh and blood grow and bone is strengthened in proportion.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he said: the breastfeeding that creates prohibition is that which occurs within the two years, for Allah says: ﴿وَالْوَالِدَاتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أَوْلَادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرَّضَاعَةَ﴾, "and mothers shall suckle their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the suckling." What occurs after the two years is not breastfeeding and creates no prohibition. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) said: "لَا رِضَاعَ بَعْدَ فِطَامٍ," "There is no breastfeeding after weaning."

It is narrated from Ali, Abu Jafar, and Abu Abd Allah (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) concerning a woman who gives her husband her milk to drink in order, by that pretense, to make herself forbidden to him, or who gives it to her bondswoman, or nurses her, to make her forbidden to him: they said (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that the man should discipline his wife, but that this creates no prohibition for him, because the breastfeeding of an adult is not breastfeeding. If a man is suckled after two years have passed from his birth, or a wife gives her husband her milk to drink, nothing is thereby made forbidden. But whatever occurs before the two years, whether by suckling, or by drinking a woman's milk, or by its being administered into the throat (wajur) or the nose (saut), is breastfeeding.

They said (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ): the milk of the stallion creates prohibition, meaning the milk attributed to the man who fathered it. This is when a man has several wives, or umm-walad mothers, in his household, and one of them nurses a slave boy while another nurses a slave girl: the two become siblings through breastfeeding, even though they did not nurse at the breast of one woman, because the one father unites them and they were nursed by the milk of his wives, so the milk is attributed to him.

Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali (ع) was asked about the wife of a man who nursed a slave girl: is it lawful for his son by another woman to marry her? He said: No. It was said to him: does she then stand to him as a sister through breastfeeding? He said: Yes, from the father's side. He said: a man had two wives, each of whom bore a son, and one of the two wives nursed a slave girl belonging to other people. He said: the other son may not marry this slave girl, for she was nursed by the milk of the same father, and what lineage forbids, breastfeeding forbids.

He (ع) was asked about a slave girl belonging to a man, whom his wife, or the mother of his child, claimed to have nursed. He said: she is not to be believed, for she is drawing something to herself. Concerning a woman who said she had nursed a slave boy and a slave girl and then denied it, he said: if she denies it, that stands. It was said to him: and if she afterward retracts her denial and claims again that she nursed them? He said: she is not to be believed. The testimony of a single upright woman is accepted in matters of breastfeeding; but if no upright woman is available, her testimony alone does not suffice.

They (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) forbade seeking a wet-nurse whose milk comes of fornication, as with a woman who commits adultery and bears a child by it: such a woman should not be sought as a wet-nurse, nor taken as a foster-nurse (zir), neither she nor her daughter born of adultery. Yet they permitted seeking a wet-nurse among polytheist women if they are within a marriage, while disliking the seeking of a wet-nurse from the milk of those known for enmity toward the family of Muhammad ((ع) and his family). Breastfeeding by the milk of fornication makes nothing forbidden. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: unlawful milk does not render the lawful unlawful, as with a woman nursed first by lawful milk and afterward by the milk of fornication. He said: whoever nurses a girl with the milk of fornication does not thereby make it forbidden to marry her, because unlawful milk does not render the lawful forbidden.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he ruled concerning a man who married a woman, gave her her dowry, and had not yet consummated the marriage, after which it was established that there was a nursing relationship between them: she must return to him what she had taken. And it was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) that he forbade women to nurse freely those boys whom they do not know.

On the Marriage of Bondswomen (Nikah al-Ima)

> وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلًا أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَتِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَنُكُم مِّن فَتَيَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَتِ

Allah Almighty said: ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلًا أَن يَنكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُم مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, up to His saying ﴿ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنكُمْ ۚ وَأَن تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾: "And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess, of your believing bondswomen," up to His saying, "That is for him among you who fears falling into sin; and that you be patient is better for you, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful."

It was narrated from Ali (ع), commenting on the words of Allah Almighty ﴿ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنكُمْ﴾, "That is for him among you who fears falling into sin," that he said: this means adultery, nothing else. So a free Muslim should not marry a bondswoman until he fears being overcome by desire and cannot find the means to marry a free woman. If he has the means to a free woman, he should not marry a bondswoman; and if he does not fear falling into sin, he likewise should not marry her, for Allah Almighty has permitted free men the marriage of bondswomen only upon these two conditions.

Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: a free man may not marry a bondswoman until two conditions are joined in him, the fear of sin and the lack of means. If he is driven to it, let him marry her. When a free man marries a bondswoman, the children she bears him belong to her master as slaves, unless he stipulates at the marriage that whatever children she bears him shall be free; if he stipulates that, they are free, and the ruling on the child follows the ruling on the mother, in freedom and in bondage. If a slave marries a free woman, their children are free, and his master may not stipulate that the free woman's children be slaves, as he might with the children of a bondswoman, because the freeing of a bondswoman's children rests with their master, who frees them if he wishes. A woman may not take ownership of her own children while they are free, nor may anyone else.

A bondswoman may not be given in marriage except with the permission of her master, for Allah says: ﴿فَانكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾, "So marry them with the permission of their families." If a bondswoman is jointly owned by two men, she is not lawful to either of them, even if the other permits it, because the part of a person cannot be divided, nor made lawful by gift. If one of the two gives her in marriage without the permission of his partner, the marriage is not valid unless the other ratifies it, and the husband may not consummate it until the second owner permits the marriage; if he does not permit it, the marriage is dissolved. Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about a bondswoman jointly owned by two men, one of whom gives her in marriage while the other is absent: is the marriage valid? He said: if the absent owner is averse to it, it is not valid.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he said: it is not lawful for a free Muslim to marry a Jewish or a Christian bondswoman, for Allah Almighty says ﴿مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, "of your believing bondswomen." Likewise a free man should not marry a Magian or a polytheist bondswoman; for were that lawful, the polytheists would come to enslave the children of the Muslims. If a man wishes to marry a bondswoman, let him free her first, and then marry her if he wishes and she wishes. The Messenger of Allah ((ع) and his family) married Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab and drew the veil (حِجَاب) over her. Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: any man who frees his slave woman and wishes to marry her, let it be with witnesses and an appointed dower; and if he makes her emancipation her dower, that is permitted, as I have explained in the foregoing.

A woman under a contract of emancipation (mukatabah) may be married with the permission of her master. Ali (ع) was asked about the marriage of a mukatabah, and he said: she may marry; and whatever child is born to her during her contract of emancipation stands in her own position, so that of that child what is freed in her is freed, and what remains in bondage in her remains in bondage. We shall mention in the chapter on those under emancipation contracts how this is reckoned, if Allah wills.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he said concerning a man who marries a bondswoman over a free wife: they are to be separated, and he is charged her dower for what he made lawful of her person if he consummated the marriage; if he did not consummate it, she is owed nothing. Abu Abd Allah Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) said: if a man marries a free woman alongside a bondswoman and the free woman knows of it, he may divide his time, two portions to the free woman and one portion to the bondswoman. If the free woman did not know that he had a bondswoman when he married her, and afterward learns of it, she has the choice: if she wishes she may remain, and if she wishes she may leave his bond, and she is owed the dower for what he made lawful of her person if he consummated the marriage; but if he did not consummate it and she chooses to part from him, she is owed nothing.

It was narrated from him that he said: it is not lawful for a free man to marry a bondswoman by herself. If he marries a free woman and a bondswoman in a single contract, one looks to whose name began the contract: if the free woman's name began it, the marriage of the bondswoman is void; but if the bondswoman's name began it and the free woman accepts to remain alongside her, the marriage of both is established, provided the man is one for whom the marriage of bondswomen is lawful, as we have described. A man may contract marriage upon a free woman while lacking the means for her dower; but if he does have the means, the marriage of the bondswoman is void, whether he began with her or named her second. Likewise, if it is not known with which of them the marriage of the bondswoman began, the marriage of the bondswoman is invalid.

He was asked about the maintenance (نَفَقَة) of a bondswoman wife. He said: when a free man marries a bondswoman, she serves her people by day and comes to her husband by night, and he owes her maintenance when they do this; but if they bar her from him by night, he owes her no maintenance.

Jafar ibn Muhammad (ع) was asked about a man who has young children who own a slave girl: may he lie with her? He said: if he desires her, let him set a just value upon himself for her, so that her price stands against him as a debt to his children; then he owns her and may lie with her if he wishes. But if the children are grown, she is not lawful to him unless they sell her to him, and it is not lawful for him to do otherwise. A man has no right to any part of his child's wealth except by the child's own goodwill, save that, if he is driven to it, he may eat of it what sustains him, in the customary measure and without indulgence, when he is in hardship and the child is wealthy.

It was narrated from him (ع) that he was asked about a man who had a slave girl, and his wife, fearing he would take her for himself, ordered her son to lie with her, and he did. He said: she has sinned, and her son has sinned, and the son is liable to the prescribed punishment (hadd) if he is an adult. And he disliked that men should approach her, even though she is thereby forbidden to the master, because the unlawful does not render the lawful forbidden.

It was narrated from Ali (ع) that he disliked a man's lying with a bondswoman over whom another holds a stipulated right. The mudabbarah may be married with the permission of her master, and her ruling remains that of a bondswoman until her master dies, whereupon she is freed. If a bondswoman is freed while she has a husband: if her husband is free, she remains his wife and has no choice; but if he is a slave, she has the choice, upon being freed, to remain with him or to leave.

The matter of the freed slave woman is settled by what the Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, did with Barirah. She was a slave woman married to a slave man, and she was grieved by her situation. When she was set free, the Messenger of Allah, (ع), gave her the choice, and she chose herself rather than her husband. He then ordered her to observe a waiting period of three menstrual cycles. And he said, (ع): if her master assists her to fulfill her emancipation contract, even if she is elderly, she has no right of choice against her husband on account of that assistance.

**The marriage of slaves**

Allah, exalted be the One who speaks, said: ﴿ عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ ﴾, "A slave who is owned and has no power over anything" (al-Nahl: 75). The Messenger of Allah, (ع) and his family, forbade a slave to marry without the permission of his master. He said: any free woman who gives herself in marriage to a slave without the permission of her guardian has made her person unlawful and is owed no dower, meaning if the master denies the marriage. But if the master permits his slave to marry, then it is valid, and the dower falls upon the master when he is content with it.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), was asked about a man who marries his own slave woman to one of his male slaves. He said: he says, "I have given her to you in marriage," and he gives her some small thing as a dower. The right of separation remains in the hand of the master: if he wishes he may part them without a divorce, and if he sells the slave man, that selling is itself a separation between them; and if he sells them together, the buyer may part them if he wishes.

Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع), said: if a slave woman is sold and she has a free husband, she remains his wife, and her person is not lawful to the buyer until her husband divorces her or dies and she completes her waiting period. From Ali, (ع): if a woman comes to own her husband, or any portion of him, the marriage between them is dissolved by the ownership itself, and she becomes the owner of her own person. It is not lawful for a woman to marry her own slave unless she first frees him; if she wishes, she may free him and then marry him afterward.

From Jafar ibn Muhammad, (ع): the slave may purchase and may approach of the slave women whatever his master has permitted him, and he may not marry more than two free women. He may marry four slave women, and the divorce of those he marries rests in the hand of his master, who may divorce them on his behalf whenever he wishes.

**The marriage of polytheists**
